Mass Effect is a great game with alot to offer. When I started the game and noticed the Codex, I was surprised how much lore they put in the whole game. I didn't expect to see a full biography of each alien race, their physiology, culture and history. Heck, if you explore the world long enough, I bet you'll know the odds and ends of everything in the galaxy,
The story itself is pretty straightforward with a nice twist. I'll not say much about it since I fear I'll spoil it.
The gameplay is pretty good, although it took me a while to get used to the controls, not to mention the tank controls of the car you get to drive on mid-game. The car is pretty sweet, even with its weird habit of breaking the laws of physics.
As you progress in the game, you'll gain companions who each have their own specialties, some are good in combat, some  use bionics - I like to call them psykers, it's an easier term - and others are good with tech.
In combat all three specialties are useful and can give the player a lot of options in tactics, but  feel like the fights get a little too easy as you approach the end of the game, and you can just charge the enemies head on.
The game isn't completely free from flaws, however.
The most common problem I had was how the voices were either too silent or too loud. Too often I heard characters talking in such a quiet tone that I could hardly hear them, even if I was standing right next to them, or even talking to them. It may not even be a bug, but it was most certainly bugging me.
The second problem I encountered were some strange graphical issues that rendered objects and characters into black boxes. I've uploaded a few screenshots to show examples. The bug can be fixed with a simple console commend, and the bug itself occurs in only specific areas, so it wasn't that much of a problem.
TL;DR - See that mountain? You CAN climb it, with a little effort. And watch for the Thresher Maws.

I have no words to sum up my feelings for Mass Effect, as it might be one of the most nostagic games i have ever played in such a short amount of time between playthroughs. about 2 years ago i got the mass effect collection on PS3 and dived in not knowing what to expect. It changed my view of every game forever, the music, the characters, the relationships, the combat, the parts the when all those were mixed together to make an anthem pounding in my ears as i mowed down geth to stop the invasion and made command with my mates as they stood by my side and risked the galaxy's fate in our hands. It. Was. Incredible. Go to 2015 as i looked on the store to see ME 1 and 2 for a combo of 10 dollars... i couldnt resist. My hands trembled as i loaded up the game heard the music, and almost started laughing as an experience of 2 years ago was making me feel like i was about to experience something that i havent done in 10+ years... and i clicked new game. It all came back, the music, Garrus with a shotgun, banter between Wrex, my hate for Ash, my romance with Liara, and it made me laugh, cry, tense up and i will never forget the experiences i have with this particular game.

A.R.E.S. is what you get when you mix Megaman, 80's cartoons, and the old DoS game "Abuse", and put them all in a 2.5D blender.
A brief review for a brief game, A.R.E.S. can typically be finished in one sitting, which of course is the point. Weapon purchases and upgrades transfer over with every new game that is started, and there are multiple endings depending on the difficulty one chooses, throwing in a little bit of bullet hell style progression into the mix as well. And for you OCD types, there's also some collection elements, so it's fun to go back and suss out secrets from every corner you can find.
If I had one complaint about this game, it's that you absolutely should be playing with a controller. I realize that isn't much to ask in this day and age, but for those stuck on a mouse and keyboard, unfortunately the programming of the game will only allow you to press two keys at once, so for some of those tricker platforming sections, it gets a little extra hard to navigate properly.
That aside, the game runs smoothly, looks nice, has a bit of a cartoonish feel to the plot, and is mostly just an excuse to run around and cause robots to explode. And at the end of the day, isn't that all we all really want?

ARES is an interesting game and is definately worth a look despite some of the negative reviews you might see. It's a side scrolling action game, very similar to Mega Man. The game's story is not it's strong point; essentially you're a robot sent on a mission to a space station to stop the evil AI from blowing up a planet. Typical stuff.
The gameplay is standard run 'n' gun for the most part, and features an upgrade system where all of your weapons can be upgraded to make them stronger. Although usually this doesn't seem to be worth it as the differences in damage are minimal. Besides what you should do is to take those components for upgrading and use them to make medkits for healing; with enough of them the game becomes a breeze since all enemies drop components.
Of course there is a higher difficulty setting, and rankings for each stage if you're a completionist. It's not the best game out there but it isn't the worst either, and recommended if you have some cash to spare and some time to kill.

Pillars of Eternity is an isometric CRPG from the studio that brought us Fallout: New Vegas and South Park: The Stick of Truth. One night you are travelling with a caravan through an area north of the Gilded Vale. The caravan stops for everyone to rest and you go out to get water for the group, you return to find a group of mercenaries who have killed all but one member of the caravan, a strange phenomenon occurs and you are forced to flee through a cave. When you reach the other side you find a strange ritual taking place and when it is complete, something about you is different. In Pillars of Eternity you must venture through Eora to find out what this change is and how you can reverse it.
PoE is set in the fictional realm of Eora. Eora is full of different factions and races and as you play the game you will discover how they link to each other and why as well as discovering the rest of Eora's deep and incredibly well thought out lore.
A couple of things to note before you carry on reading my review. Firstly I have not finished this game at the time of writing my review, I'd say I'm about a fifth of the way in but I feel like I've experienced enough of it to write a detailed review. Secondly this is the first time I have properly played a CRPG and so I'm inexperienced with this type of game so some of my opinions may differ from CRPG veterans.
+Great graphics and well designed emvironments though the character models aren't the best
+A reasonably detailed character creator with a number of different races, classes and backgrounds to choose from
+An interesting main plot as well as some interesting side quests
+There's a hell of a lot to do, as mentioned previously at 16 hours playtime I'm only around a fifth of the way through all of the content on offer
+Due to the game's reputation system and side quests with different possible endings you can create your own story when playing PoE even though the outcome is the same
+Fantastic writing, in particular the interaction of different characters who feel real due to how good the writing is, e.g. how they respond to what is being said
+Some great voice acting
+As mentioned before Eora has very deep lore and finding out about it over the course of the game and through the Digital Collector's book is fascinating
+The combat is simple yet rewarding and you really have to think about who should attack who and with what so that you are successful, especially when fighting large groups
+Eight different companions to find and team up with over the course of the game, each of a different class with unique abilities to help you in a fight
+All eight companions have interesting backstories and all have a reason for being where you found them which is good to see
+Relatively early in the game you get possesion of a rundown stronghold and you can restore it to its former glory, I absolutely love that kind of thing in games so I thoroughly enjoyed building it back up
+The different locations in the game are rather large and each one either has or is linked to a fair few sidequest though the map looks a bit empty as there aren't too many different locations
+Outstanding soundtrack and great sound effects throughout
+The game's difficulty can be changed throughout
+Big heads mode, thanks Josh!
-Voice acting is used sporadically, the main characters all have their own voice actors yet most of their dialogue is unvoiced and you have to read it, I felt that it often broke the flow of dialogue as one section would be voiced and the next wouldn't be with seemingly no method behind it
-As mentioned previously the character models don't look great
-Frequent loading screens which take a long time
-There's a Kickstarter backer only achievement so unless you backed it you can't get 100%
This covers the Royal Edition of the game, the first five are also available in the Champion edition. I will cover them in the order that they appear on the store page.
+The OST is, as mentioned, fantastic
+/-The Campaign Almanac is interesting but the font is difficult to read
+The Digital Game Map is very nice and has a good amount of detail though it has a bit of a strange resolution
+/-The Making Of Documentary isn't available yet
-The Wallpapers are all very nice but they all have strange resolutions and aren't available in 1920x1080
-The ringtones are nice little sound clips but I don't think you'd want them set as your phone's ringtone, most of them are soundclips of a character speaking
+/-The Digital Novella isn't available yet
+The Digital Collector's Book is very good and goes into great detail when explaining the game's lore
+The Concept art is absolutely fantastic and very high quality, I thoroughly enjoyed looking through it
+The Digital Strategy guide is very helpful and well written
Verdict:
9.5
A truly outstanding isometric CRPG with great graphics, an extremely well-written story, good combat and rich lore to back it all up. If you're a fan of CRPGs you've done yourself a disservice by not picking this game up sooner.

This may turn into a somewhat lengthy review, so if you don't wanna read all that sh#t here's the bottom line first: This game is boring. There, I said it.
First of all, let me say that I've been anticipating this game for about 2 years, having been a huge fan of the Baldur's Gate series for many years before that. This isn't a case of the concept being new to me, or that I was expecting an action game. It's not even a bad game. If you're genuinely enjoying this game I'm not here to tell you that you shouldn't. I will share with you, however, why I'm not thrilled.
I have probably spent half of my entire gaming life in the BG series. After playing it so much, and having watched it age, it has become apparent that there are many aspects of the game that could be improved upon. When I think "spiritual succesor to Baldur's Gate released in 2015" I get certain expectations. Expectations I feel were not met.
Foremost of all, is that the game is flat out boring. The game fails to create an interesting or immersive world. Too much of the game is presented in written form (i.e. prepare to read a LOT.) I can't say I have a problem with reading, but I found myself being bored often while reading what the game was serving up. I always felt like I was playing a game; it never took me to another place in my mind. All the lore was standard and uninspired. I'd rather it were set in a classic world we know and love as opposed to this hollow one.
It doesn't help that in Dialogue, you can't tell how much longer the latest uninteresting NPC is going to babble on for.
Too much of the written content is either wholly unnecessary or could have been presented in a more interesting and visual way. Instead of giving me a mini essay to read on the appearance of the huge sharkwoman warrior, how about making the character models more interesting and expressive? i.e. SHOW me.
**MINOR SPOILER: Another example, when Raedric was offering me the chance to join him, I had lost all interest in the "story" of the quest. All I had to go on was two characters giving speeches. I just wanted him to shut up and for this boring quest to be over. **
Why did I travel all the way across to the other side of this room just to click on a magnifying glass and read "Rats scurry in between the cracks of the stairs." or something banal like that. The game is littered with these useless nothings.
The look of the in-game world is bland and uninteresting to me. It reminds me of a cross between Diablo 2 and Icewind Dale 2 in terms of atmosphere. I was never a fan of those games, precisely because they felt "lifeless" to me. Character appearance customization is something RPG gamers typically enjoy. Too many games fail to give us the fun we seek in this regard. The Infinity engine games failed, and so does Pillars.
Speaking of a lack of improvements: All my old frustrations are still there. Namely characters getting in each other's way during combat, small and claustrophobic areas making for messy gameplay, poor selection of roleplaying options, etc.
In a visually appealing sense, there is very little upgrade from the old Infinity Engine games. Yes, the graphics are "better." More advanced, smoother. Water looks nice. But there's nothing that's done really well. In a lot of ways, Pillars of Eternity feels like an old game. That's not necessarily a bad thing, I just think there's actually better old games out there. Games that managed to create a visually appealing environment despite graphical limitations.
One thing games like this always seem to fail in is visual presentation of populated areas. NPCs look particularly stiff (notice there isn't a single patron in the Gilded Vale tavern that's sitting down? WTF?). Oh and the choreographed movement of your party... ugh that's gross! Baldur's Gate actually did it quite well for the time. NPC models seemed more organic. I remember how alive the actual city of Baldur's Gate felt when I was exploring it for the first time. In this, and many other aspects, Baldur's Gate left a lot to the imagination. But it stimulated the imagination and took it in specific directions. Pillars on the other hand, is just dull. Or maybe I'm just getting old and not so easily amused any more.
There's plenty I find frustrating with the in game mechanics too. Like why can't I use stealth with just one party member? Why is my whole party stealthed? What's the purpose of making the entire party move slower when stealthed? As a seasoned BG player I thought the game mechanics would be fairly intuitive for me, but I haven't been able to figure out the stealth system or some of the decisions that went into making it.
I remember in an interview one of the devs was very enthused about how all the stats would actually matter and be helpful now, and how it would allow for unexpected and interesting character builds. Well, to be fair, the first part of that is kinda true. All the stats matter in certain ways now, which is nice. But I tried to make a smart and wise barbarian the first time I loaded up. Let's just say I had to restart the game.
What's the purpose of limiting your party to 2 sets of camping supplies? All it does is make the game less fun for me.
The party NPCs are just not memorable. Granted, I haven't got very far in their individual quests yet...but here's the thing: I don't really care to either. Baldur's Gate had memorable NPCs that oozed personality.
I could go on but I think that's enough. I may end up finishing the game and putting a lot of hours into it. But that's only because I've waited a long time and there's nothing better. I've had some decent fun on it too, but my initial excitement has waned.

Before even starting the game, I realized that the character creation was pretty lacking, with very few options and the ones that were available were pretty♥♥♥♥♥♥ I settled with my bright pink neanderthal with a mohawk and jumped in to the world. You start out next to a charred skeleton, some starting gear and a book which you can read and learn a bit of the back story to the area of the game. I have mixed feelings about these books. I feel like the guy who designed this feature is one of those people who reads the quest giver text in MMO's. Seriously who the ♥♥♥♥ does that? It is kinda dull to stop and read a lot of text, especially if you are freezing your♥♥♥♥♥off and slowly dying of hunger. But there are some certain situations in the game that make this kinda cool - I'll explain more on that later. You quickly learn that you are on a snow covered island where you need to hunt for food, keep warm and ideally build shelters and better armor and weapons to progress to new areas of the island. I do like the idea of progression, with enemies further in the game getting tougher and requiring you to fully explore each crafting tier before moving on or potentially getting your head beaten in by a Silver Surfer or mini Maokai. But it does make it a tiny bit grind-ish by forcing you to collect a large number of materials to make the required gear. This is made even worse if you are playing co-op or in a group as the mining nodes have set locations and respawn times, so you may end up fighting each other for them or having to wait. We did find one solution to quickly get some crafting materials early in the game. You can build houses and shelters to keep yourself warm and your items safe and there are a few little pre-generated unfinished villages around the map. One creative way to keep yourself warm is that you can actually set these half-built houses on fire! Not only that but after they burn down they spew out precious resources that you can then re-use to make armor or new houses.
As with most survival games, you get thrown in to the game with very little explanation of what to do. Luckily the intro to the game has been very carefully set up. There is a small town within view that you can head over to and easily figure out that these buildings are incomplete and you need to craft nails and wooden boards to finish them off. The wooden boards are easily - make axe, cut trees, get wood, make boards. The nails took us a bit longer to figure out.. You can click on the item in the crafting window and it tells you what items you need to craft it. You need tin to make nails, you need a smelter to make tin from tin ore and coal.. but where the ♥♥♥♥ do you get tin ore and coal! We eventually noticed some ore deposits around the place, where you can get tin, coal, etc. But we had no idea how to mine them! Turns out, the tool required for mining is a Hammer. Why the ♥♥♥♥ a hammer.. c'mon. I think there are two things to do to help new players here; Firstly, the text on the item that says "Used for Mining" is the same color as the rest of the flavor text and blends in. Perhaps making it a different colour would help new players spot what it's used for. Secondly, don't make it a ♥♥♥♥ing hammer! What's wrong with pickaxe?
Shortly after settling down in our ♥♥♥♥♥♥ village, we were filled with a sense of dread after hearing loud roars in the distance and after looking up seeing a big ♥♥♥♥ing dragon breathing fire on a tower. Now i've read other people's accounts and apparently the dragon has come and laid waste to them all, but even after shooting arrows at him in an attempt to♥♥♥♥♥♥him off he still hasn't paid us a visit. I have always been one to take on a challenge, so the big♥♥♥♥♥dragon is kinda a cool feature. It makes me want to get better gear and slay that ♥♥♥♥er. Behind the village is a little cotton farm which you can harvest to make bandages. I think its explosive cotton because the sound effect when you harvest it sounds like small explosions. Luckily there is enough cotton to make a comfortable number of bandages for two people, but tough♥♥♥♥♥♥if you are playing in a larger group. Again, you may need to turn your volume down or risk becoming permanently deaf as crafting the bandages sounds like metal banging together inside your ear drum. Food on the starting island quickly runs out, forcing you to move on to the next main island where you are met with a sharp increase in the level of challenge the game offers. You are soon surrounded by tasty antelope and rabbits that you can eat, but also giant blue cats and skeletons that can eat you. The AI is a bit frustrating here because if you stand still you can see that all of the enemies are slowly gravitating towards you.. eventually getting close enough to sprint at you and wreck your day. Luckily they attack slowly, because if they hit you you're ♥♥♥♥ed. You can only take one or two hits because most likely you skipped the tin and copper tier armor because there is just not enough ores on the starting island to make them!
We eventually stumbled upon a little town that was completely built! It made us wonder why the ♥♥♥♥ we built up the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ town when we could have just lived here. We grabbed all of our loot from the old place and moved in, even though it felt a little too good to be true. We noticed that there was one of those books that we never read in the town so we decided to read it. It explained that the previous villagers had all evacuated because the town was haunted and that something still lingered. Well,♥♥♥♥♥♥ Sure enough, that night the town filled up with ghost skeletons that wanted to put their cold bony fingers in our butt holes. ♥♥♥♥ it, too late, we settled. We have just accepted the fact that we have to brawl skeletons each night. After gathering up enough food to survive and ores to make bronze armor, we went for a wander. We found giant trees that wanted to eat us, green lumberjacks, Gollum, Shrek and a really cool teleporting doorway! It looked like you were going in to some ruins but when you went through you were actually on the other side of the map in another ruins. It's actually a pretty awesome feature! All of these cool little finds makes me want to explore the game even more.
Apart from the pretty buggy AI, teleporting enemies, characters glitching through the floor, getting stuck on terrain, terrible sound effects, character animation being really♥♥♥♥♥♥. the game actually has some very solid game play. I think it does have a fair way to go but looking back at other games like Minecraft and Rust that looked ♥♥♥♥♥♥, but actually had solid game play.. Those games have come a long way and are now really awesome. I think that with a bit of attention this game could definitely be one to look out for. If you want to jump on the bandwagon early then you can grab it at an awesome price right now on the Humble Bundle website. Definitely advise checking it out if you have the time to play as it does take a little bit of time to get in to.

I was in high school and heard about the Homestuck Kickstarter. I was ecstatic. I got into college and remained excited. I graduated college, and remained hopeful. Hiveswap arrived. And all is forgiven.
I'm the kind of guy that goes into games exploring and checking everything possible. I've played point-and-click games Venus, where I get disappointed when I'm constantly barraged by the same soundclip of the protagonist saying "I can't do that". When I began playing Hiveswap, I was astounded. I got stuck in Joey's room for a full hour. And not because of a puzzle, but from my own volition. I tried every single item and hotspot combination. And I was fascinated by what I read. I became satisfied when I began getting achievements for trying seemingly innocuous combinations, which was super satisfying. After 8 hours, across a couple of days, I managed to finish Act 1. I was extremely satisfied. I even tried my hand at playing the game all over again, this time skipping all the flavor text. It took me around 15 minutes. That's when I realized my first playthrough was exactly how this game is squeezed out of its content.
I for one found myself relieved with the change of graphics from 3D to 2D. It feels so much more like Homestuck in that way.
The music is just absolutely marvelous. I found myself tapping my foot, my knees, humming along with the music in each room. Even the characters, I gotta say, are a big step up from the source material. Through the constant use of the items and skills in the characters' sylladexes and strife specibi, I got to understand their motivations. Joey's feelings against POGs, Bubsy and her father as well as Xefros' feelings towards his own hobbies and culture.
I really can't wait to see what comes next. 5 years of waiting were worth it, at least for me.

Absolutely wonderful game. You have big boss/creatures battles, which you can tackle in multiple ways, you can climb them holding on for dear life and hacking away at them, you can stay at a distance throwing spells or shooting arrows, or you can just send in your pawns to do the work. The pawns are your 3 AI companions, one pawn is your own and you can customize it any way you choose, and it learns from how you play or tell it to play and tries to follow that. The other 2 pawns are ones other people have created as their main pawns, and you can summon them to your world. You can not customize them, but you can switch them out easily.
There are 9 different classes in the game and it is very easy to switch between them, even with the most basic skills they are good enough if you let your pawns pick up the slack. You're not locked in into your choice as with most other RPGs and in fact it is beneficial to explore the classes as you can pick up some skills which are class specific but carry over across all classes (augments). That's why you will be able to find just the play style that most suits you. Your main pawn can also switch classes in the same way, there is only a slightly smaller class selection for them.
The story is interesting enough, but it isn't really explored much. Mostly you're just picking up quests in the hub areas and going out into the open world to complete them. Which is fine, until you're returning to the same exact spot for the 8th time and you have to run all the way there every time. There is the possibility of fast travel, but it's limited to where you can fast travel, you can find Portcrystals and set them down somewhere in the world, then you can fast travel to there any time you choose. However you would need to know the game to know where the best spots for placing them are. Thankfully the monsters you encounter on the way have a varied style of fighting, it's just a shame that the monster variety doesn't improve until after you've "beaten" the game.
This is a great game, hampered by the feeling that it wants you to do the same thing over and over again, and that's really where you have to know if you can endure the grind or not. Although just going through the main game will not be too repetitive, anything past that and it's Grind City all the way.
8 / 10

I really wanted to love this game. In a way I still very like it, but in 2016, where there are games far better I simply cannot recommend it.
Who is this game for? Probably for people who enjoy monster slashing, especially bosses fights. Yes! That is what shines here, but it also does not at the same time. Every single time when you travell, you meet the same bunch of monsters in the same places. At first it is not annoying, but after a while, when you have to go the same route for yet another and another and another and another and another time... You simply know every single time you will be attacked, you will have to fight and already know how to do it. There is no surprise here. Monsters simply respawn after you leave the area! Your killings are insignificant.
On the other hand, when you fight them, especially during night time, when you cannot actually see them all, and they call reinforcements, it's just fun! You fight, kill, more come, more die and there seems to be no stopping to it and yet, after a while, when you return to area, they are there again. Waiting to be slaughtered by your might.
Ohhh yes for You are mighty after a while! They are not even a challenge, just sheeps ready fo slaughter. Boss fights on the other hand can be too challenging at the beggining but after a while you just grab, press the same buttons for a while and slaughter them like they had no meaning at all.
I love the design of areas, darkness in dungeons, they are trully perfect. When you dwell in ruins, catacoombs etc. you can trully enjoy your time. It is in a way similar to Dark Souls, sometimes you can't know where your feet take you. On the other hand journey to these places can waste you so much time, you simply don't want to explore it anymore...
But if above does NOT bother you, you may find a lot of fun in this game UNLESS! Yes, unfortunately there are two other major things which infuriate me. First is the terrible User Interface. Oh dear... DO you perhaps remember Gothic 1? Many people accused it of having the worst UI ever. Imagine that this game is even worse then this... It's purely work of evil! You have to navigate through countless pages eg. to exit the game you have to exit to menu, then click to enter the menu, wait few seconds for it to load, click exit the game, approve of exiting and finally! And its just when you want to quit it. Please don't make me describe how it works during gameplay...
Where UI was not a strong point of Gothic, story is where it shined. Story of Dragons Dogma shines... NOT! It's terrible, generic and soooo much disappointing. If you don't care for story, for making the same stupid quests in the same places for the same rewards, want to smash enemies and kill boss or two, then it's the game made specificly for you. But when you expect an RPG to be a ROLE playing game with deep story, many choices in open world, stay away from it, as story sounds fancy, but execution is sooo lack luster. Yeez!
Buy it on sale maybe, buy if you don't have anything else to play, but be prepared for a game, which could easily beat a lot of games, but was soo terribly executed.

I don't understand the positive reviews.
To me, the worst part of this game is what the developers did to your companions, the "Pawns". They have litterally no personality. It's right there in the game, it tells you this. So why bother with them at all? Why make them human-looking when they could have been awesome golems or robots and still carry the same weight story- and lorewise?
And you can't control them, at all. No scripts like in Dragon Age, no pause -> issue commands -> watch them happen or top down tactical menu for increased battlefield overview and control. Nope, nothing but three different generic commands that don't work.
Shame.
Other than that, I agree to what other people are saying about the "open world". Yes, you can explore places... but you will die. There is no visible level indicators on the enemies so, when I wandered off into the wilderness and encountered my first bandits or lizardmen I thought "Aha, my army of magic Pawn-people and I, the chosen one, can handle this!". I could not. I was one- or two-shot to death. Again, and again, and again. With no "quicksave-key" it gets tedious to save all the time you explore in case you suddenly encounter an enemey that is too strong but has nothing to give this away to the player.
There are so many more things in this game that are just poor design choices but I won't go in to them. Instead, if you want to see what people who play it a lot and got invested enough to actually care did, check the mod scene. If you disregard all the nude-mods, most mods involve "no carry limit", "no stamina drain when running" and changing the way leveling shapes your character.
Don't buy it. Instead try Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning, much better in every way, or The Last Remnant. The Last Remnant has a similar "not directly controlling your companions in battle" thing, but is better.

First i am going to say that i am conflicted on this game. And lastly, the controlls are just awful. If you are like me, which i assume you are, you played the previous dynasty warriors games on a console and are familiar with the controls. If not, then you're not going to be as bothered by this. If you use a gamepad (which you honestly should for a game like this), it is very important to know...that some genius at KOEI decided it would be a FANTASTIC idea to make the musou button (special ability) and confirm button the exact same button. Allow me to explain the layout of the controller for this game on console so you can better understand (will use a 360 controller for demonstration, and for a reference of those who would like to use the most effective layout.)
Left analog stick= move
Right analog stick= camera
A= jump/confirm
B=Musou/back
X= normal attack
Y= Strong attack
LB= Block
LT= Change weapon
RB= Call horse
RT= Map
Start= Start
Back=? (i forgot what it did but it doesnt matter)
Directional Buttons= bodyguard commands
So we see here we have a pretty effective set up on console. Heres where KOEI innovated the game for PC gamers.
Musou and confirm are the same button, so if you want to get anywhere navigation wise you need to press B to confirm. Which is awkward and weird
Jump is also linked to the back button. So by pressing A you will end up going back in the menus which is also awkward and confusing for those familiar with the gamepad
In order to naviagte specific menus left and right, you need to press the Block button (LB) and the change weapon button (LT) where on console it was just LT and RT, so again ♥♥♥♥ing awkard.
And the best part, the game doesnt tell you which key to press for either M/K or gamepad!!! it just shows you a ♥♥♥♥ing logo of what you should press.
Oh and also, they added a pause button which is a diversion and doesnt do anything. The real pause button is called bring up display or some♥♥♥♥♥♥ So the pause button is useless.
So you will need to decide if you are familiar with the controls from console between an effective combat control system, or an effective navigation system. Because some sociopath at KOEI decided that we cant have both. So definitly keep that in mind when you go to play this game. Oh and when using the gamepad, the main menu says "press any key to countinue". Which is a gigantic lie. You need to press whichever button you assigned to the "display battle or whatever the ♥♥♥♥" button (not pause).
Despite these issues and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t, it is a good port and it plays how it should. after a while i adjusted to the controls and am kicking♥♥♥♥♥all over the place. It may not bother you but it kind of upset me, was all the characters and character weapons are available right from the start (only the weak versions of the weapons, you still have to unlock all of those). I feel this was a terrible move because A) it takes away the excitment of unlocking characters and seeing them for the first time and which weapon they have. B) In this game you get 2 weapons...any two weapons you do so please. SO by having all the weapon types available at the start takes away the fun of unlocking them. which for me, was the best thing in dynasty warriors 8.
So i do reccomend getting the game, but i reccomend waiting a while until KOEI fixes the problems and drops the price. Hope this helped!

Truly the greatest Dynasty Warriors title to date, and quite a fine PC port overall. A mixture of PS3 and PS4 visuals, with the biggest drawback being that there is no online co-op play (yet?) for the PC version. Aside from that rather large negative though, the huge positive is how long this game will last you if you've ever been a fan of the Dynasty Warriors titles. Completing the base story-lines on my regular DW8 PS3 version had taken me roughly 30 hours. Xtreme Legends Complete Edition expands on to a new storyline featuring Lu Bu, Challenge Mode, Free Mode and further character advancement for the 80+ characters, up towards a level of 150 each - and with hundreds of weapons to find and collect. Ambition Mode has also been greatly expanded, something I had only played a few hours of on my PS3 copy of DW8 - but also another extremely fun mode for any fan of this series.
Although the console versions sometimes struggle at the FPS side of things, I've been able to maintain 60 FPS at all times regardless of how many enemies are on the screen at once. This is all whilst running at maximum-detail graphical settings, 1920 x 1080, under Windows 7. (I hear that Windows 8 is currently causing some trouble for other players, but not all.)

I like anime, but this is my first "visual novel." I made it all the way through this story, and I can't recommend it. The art is really good. The music is appropriate albeit a little repetitive. The story had some promise at first (it seemed), and had some novel ideas, but ended up just being cliché. As others have mentioned, the ending had the makings of being sad, but for me really wasn’t. Why? By the time they got around to ending it, I didn’t really care about any of the characters.
Writing was ok, but I can’t think of a scene except for the very last one that wasn’t unnecessarily drawn out way too long. I know they were trying to provide backstory and detail in an attempt to make the characters deeper, but for me there were far too many instances thinking “I wish they would just get on with it an advance the plot already…” Sometimes that wish would take as much as 30-45 minutes of drawn out dialog.
The characters themselves weren’t great. Sion was the character I liked the most, and her story was fairly sad. The male main character I didn’t care at all for. He was intentionally cold, emotionless, and flat. They tried to remedy that near the end of the story, but by then I just simply didn’t care. It was too little too late. A half an hour of opening him up at the end didn’t make up for 9.5 hours of listening to the same “poor me” lines from him again and again.
I was waiting for some action, or a big plot twist, or something. Nothing like that ever came. The story was extremely predictable from beginning to end. I'm glad that I was eventully able to reach the end, just because this is the first visual novel that I've ever experienced. It's an interesting idea, and I'm sure there are good ones out there, but I didn't think this one was particularly great. The whole story could have easily been condensed down to 2 hours and probably would have been more enjoyable, given the fact that at 10+ hours in, at the end, you wouldn't be feeling like the whole experience was such a chore.
At the end, for me the positives outweigh the negatives. I've read the positive reviews and I can see why some people liked it, but reading the negative reviews after having gone through this, I don't disagree with any of the points that they make either. 3/10.

The premise is pretty solid for this one and I think the execution does it justice, though the game does lose a bit of momentum in its second half, and the last act of the game is kind of a slog similar to sitting through a funeral. But overall, I enjoyed it. The art is good, the music is good, the story's not too long, the characters, while maybe a bit mary sue-ish, feel real enough to keep me engaged in their interactions, and the ambiguous nature of the main plot is probably for the best; doesn't really need to be an exact answer for everything. The romantic aspects are generally sidelined and only come into play near the end (maybe why the ending felt like a slog for me) but there's enough of a buildup and character development that it's not really bothersome. Do note that this is a VN with no choices whatsoever, literally just a visual novel that you read/look at/listen to etc. But it works fine for the story. So yeah. Mildly pleasant overall, doesn't really feel like it drags on much, and there's plenty of heart to it.
The heck is up with the intro though, doesn't really fit in with the tone of the game at all.

I enjoyed it. A. LOT. The lore. My god. If that's your thing, you got it, mate. This is...pretty much a Star Wars meets TPS meets RPG. I can't even tell if Star Wars has more lore to it than ME, but I get the feeling that ME gives you a MUCH bigger "schooling" feeling. No joke.
(10/10 would be homeschooled again :P)
Ok, now off to the actual deal that everyone does with video games. Let's start with the Soundtrack.
It's alright I suppose. Rather fitting for what it is. The menu theme is what really stuck me throughout the game though. Maybe that's why it's meant to be. The rest is all movie-like stuff that just fits the ambient you're in I guess.
Lore is obvious. Don't even ask how in-depth it is. So much I couldn't be asked to read it all, and I regret not reading 100% of what turians, salarians and asari are all about, I just wanted the general idea and I got it. :P
Of course, with lore, comes backstory, and I mean it. It has plenty of backstory for ya. Not as much as the sequels as I'm led to believe but it'll do.
The mechanics, like skill trees, abilities, etc. They're all perfect, imho. I can't see it in any other (better) way. The fact you unlock skills for certain classes if you use their abilities 100 times in a run kind of makes it seem null, though. I dunno.
Squadmate system...uh...Everyone says Kaidan has stupid AI but I don't really notice it. The only squadmate I had a problem with was (SPOILER ALERT) Wrex. He just stands there and doesn't shoot a lot back. Also, he loves switching to his pistol for no reason. Oh, yeah, I've used Kaidan for like, 65% of the game. Maybe more. Wrex as well.
Squadmate AI seems to be fine with most of them except Wrex, I guess. All he does is just stand there and take it unless you make him use a Shotgun, I think.
Inventory system is very well done, for its time. Bit of an issue with the fact that there IS a limit for the amount of gear you can carry though. 150. I don't think this was mentioned in the tutorials and I purposedly went looking for it once I found out you could carry stuff. Thought it was infinite. It bit me in the♥♥♥♥♥
Enemy AI? They spam a handful of lines. Trust me, it's more hilarious than annoying. Unless either you have a dull sense of humor and/or get mad easily, or, they're actually biotics stopping you from doing anything and taking damage as they yell "I'LL...DESTROY YOU!" or "ENEMIES EVERYWHERE"...oh god I'm grinning at the thought of the guy saying it again.
The AI isn't stupidly bad but not very good either. The game's difficulty only makes them either easy to fight against or hard. Just damage modifiers, really. I think so anyway.
Cover system...Not very good. Doesn't make the game unplayable though. I spent most of the time crouching to make my aim better and taking my time, sneaking. :P
But yeah, it goes as far to make you want to scream "GET THE ♥♥♥♥ OUT OF THERE SHEPARD OMFG!!!"
How good shooting feels? I dunno. I spent the game with only two weapon types, barely used one, and NEVER used the other. From the ones I've used, yes, it does feel great when you use them, especially so with the Sniper rifles.
Pistols are only pure amazing if you get to the point where you don't have to worry about overheating.
Last of the "In-game Gameplay" category (I think), the Mako.
Oh god. Space exploration IS fun but not with that..turtle-scorpion hybrid. I'll give it one thing, it is pretty damn useful for taking down just about anything. But driving it feels like telling a mule to do ANYTHING, at least, specifically, when turning the thing left or right.
And, depending on how you do things, you'll be spending most of the game with it. Yep.
Ok, onto the more...story-related stuff.
Character Development (your own)
You get to give your Shepard his/her own background, class, etc. That's what every RPG should do, because I loved this idea. Gives it so much immersion. Now add the fact it's not just the background, but also how you got so high in rank. Nice, huh?
See the tag "Choices Matter" there? Heh, we're not kidding. This game KNOWS what you did, wherever you go, whatever you do. Some higher-up will know. Or some random guy will. It all depends on the situation you're in. And there's a fair amount of those in the game. That's what makes this game such a refined RPG.
Grow to be an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Grow to be a goodie two-shoes. Grow to be corrupt but saved the galaxy anyways. Be whoever you want you (or your character) to be.
Character Development (Squadmates, Major characters, etc.)
This game...made me care deeply for my whole team. Even if I had just met them. Even if I didn't know them all too well.
They've always been there for Shepard and his/her mission to stop Saren. Even Ashley, that♥♥♥♥♥♥ I...
Yeah. They're that good. It's not easy to put it in words. *cough* They're better than Undertale's cast. *cough*
Plot...falls under backstory and lore I guess. If they bothered to write what happened BEFORE the game, then wonder what they bothered to write what happens DURING the game? :P
Though I do have to admit it feels kind of rushed near the end, what with knowing what the threat is exactly, and getting that "Just getting started" feeling. That's why it grew into a trilogy. Who knows about the next follow-ups.
I think that covers it. Stuff that makes ME what it is known as now, like, say, romance subplots, forgive me for missing them out, but I didn't do it because of ME2 and 3's different character romances. If I did, I'd be cheating on them. :P
DO NOT WATCH GAMER POOP BEFORE PLAYING ME3, I WARN YOU. It'll make a difference, believe ME! Also, has great voice acting for its rather...low pool of voice actors. I'm pleasantly surprised. Better than the use TES makes.
Anyways, yeah. Absolutely outstanding RPG. A must-play for RPG lovers, all things Sci-fi, lore, or just a good movie, ya got it! DO NOT GET IT FOR THE TPS GAMEPLAY. I honestly don't know who'd do that but that's just crazy. Don't bash on the game if you did, that's not why it's good. I mean, it is good but what makes it not-so-good is the cover system I mentioned.
I also feel like just anyone can play this. It's not one of 'those' games where you die if you do something wrong. That's only if you're playing in the hardest difficulties, which are locked in your first run, thankfully. So it's good for both casuals and RPG-specfic players.
So, yeah. If you're considering getting this game, JUST DO IT! It IS certainly worth it!...Especially so on a sale... :3

I played for about 90 minutes yesterday.
I spawned and almost immediately met another player. We teamed up and started looting the houses in the nearby town.
After finding some loot, we went into the stores and looted some more. Every time we saw another player, we would loudly talk about our (non-existing) shotguns and how we aren't afraid to use them.
After scavenging for a while and figuring out the menus together, we spotted a water tower in the distance and decided to head there. My new friend saw another player in the distance who was building a base near the water tower.
He told me to stay in the bushes and wait while he approaches him. I crouched down and hid in a nearby bush while I watched my friend talk to this guy. I could hear him say "relax, don't shoot me" after a while I heard him say "ok I have a friend with me" and I came out of the bushes.
The guy we met was almost completely naked and he told us a wolf attacked him, so he had to rip up his clothes to use as bandages. He showed us how to cut trees and build a base.
After some time, I wandered off and started looting some nearby houses and found a baseball bat. Pretty sweet.
I'd say the only thing that the game is lacking at this moment is a few more mobs. In my 90 minutes of playing, I did not encounter a single zombie or animal. Also the menus are a bit cluttered, but hey, the game is in alpha early access so that's ok.
The devs are pushing out updates pretty much weekly and the community is working on getting the game indie-funded by cry engine. I had a good time playing and will continue to play. Probably the best multiplayer experience I've had in a while.

Yes, it uses isometric view and uses a similar art style to the old games, but that's not a bad thing at all. Not everything has to be 3D or First Person to be a good game.
So far, 27h in with my strong hold secured, and half way through the endless paths (but still at the beginning of the main story) I'm really enjoying the world, the story telling and Obsidian's homebrew rpg system. It's so much better than the old D&D adaptions, as they were free to adjust those things they didn't like or that didn't fit to a CRPG, and they were free to develop their own world.
It's a classic fantasy setting, although classes and races differ somewhat. Sure, you find elves and dwarfs, wizards and fighters, but also godlike and ciphers - and front loader pistols and guns. It's got it's own spin on the genre and not for worse. The setting is somewhat gruesome though not black and white. Sure, there are bad guys, but not all are evil - some are just mad from grievance and desperation. It's a great world to explore with a lot of freedom of choice.
If you like good RPGs then this is what you should go for (also try Dininity: Original Sin, another great Kickstarter rpg game, if you haven't already).

Great game. While not innovative, it was incredibly refreshing to play a game whose sole purpose was to be fun. It's very streamlined in this sense, and it faciliates the unique nemesis system. This is truly the meat of the game. Essentially it creates unique orcs from a huge pool of traits, and makes them bosses in the world. The traits are fairly varied and the level of detail put into the orcs is astounding. The game has an upgrade system which was actually diverse and I found myself using a lot of the neat abilities you can get. All in all there's definitely a lot of fun to be had here, but there's not a lot to say about it really.
Now there's only a handful of things about this game I could criticize. I found the movie name dropping and general quoting was pretty obvious. While it's good material, it just felt odd. And while the story starts off brilliantly it then becomes erratic and hard to follow due to multiple forces pushing you each way. The last two "bosses" were just quicktime events pretty much, and the last boss would be the huge Graug as far as I consider it. Lastly the nemesis system starts to wear itself thin. Sure the orcs may look new and unique, it's really just a skin on top of the recycled quirks they have.
All in all, I'm hoping for some sort of sequel because this one had a lot of what I liked, but definitely left me wanting more. It is a very satisfying game to be sure, and I can safely say my money and time was not wasted.

The main highlight is the Nemesis System, it's something that will keep you coming back to this game every once in a while and still have lots of fun for hours. Game is pretty cheap now even when not on sale, so pick it up and have some fun, or wait for it to be on sale if you're a cheap♥♥♥♥♥like me.

If you're a megaman fan, it's a good idea to pick this one up. The stages are set up so that you're not always just rushing in one direction to the end. You find weapons and abilities that you can upgrade, as well as craft certain useable items throughout the game.
Being able to craft repair kits in stage makes the game a bit more forgiving, but you waste materials that you would rather use on upgrades. Crafting can also be a bit annoying sometimes because it feels needlessly split amongst 3 different kinds of materials, when all of them are used when crafting any item, and only the yellow ones seem to be a bit more scarce than the others. 
The slides are a little hard to execute with a controller. If you use a PS3/4 Controller using DS#Tool, it will force-bind movement to the analog stick, which might make certain movements a little more complicated than I wanted, but this could be fixed by using something like Joy2Key instead.
Despite a few nuances in the game, It was pretty fun to play. It only takes a couple hours to beat for the seasoned veteran in platformers, but there are also many things that are easily missed or passed on the first playthrough. The stage system allows you to easily revisit these areas, so it's not like you have to play through the whole game.

Being a game that was originally created for the PS3, ported to PS4 and then ported to PC, it is obvious that this game will have flaws. I bought this game knowing this, but my purchase was out of hope for the future, hope that KOEI won't port a game, but make a full on dedicated PC game with their next instalment, that is why I bought it for €50.
Story:
This is based on the book "Romance of the Three Kingdoms", when China was undergoing civil war with many warlords battling for fame, power and wealth.
The story line follows the main clans that were involved and their legendary Generals. Shu, Wei, Wu, Jin and now Lu Bu storyline.
There is a campaign for each clan that involves several major battles to complete; you can also unlock "hypothetical" scenarios for each clan. There is a wide cast of characters you can choose to play, but in campaign, you get to choose 1 out of 3 for each mission.
Mechanics:
You bring 2 weapons with to the battlefield, which could hold different properties and elements to give you an edge over your opponent.
You can equip skills to boost certain attributes from resilience to attack to speed and even level up quicker.
Musou is now accompanied by the rage bar that unleashes a whole lot of hurt on your enemy.
Flurry is like rage, but just more localized and uses elemental types to use (heaven, earth, man)
Tons of weapons to choose from
Maps are quite large than the older games and more detailed.
Not helping your allies can land you in trouble now thanks to the morale bar
Game Modes:
-Campaign: play the storyline of the clans and their battles
-Ambition Mode: fight till you house the Han (basically just fight till your heart’s content and build a village while doing so)
-Free mode: need any more explanations?
-Challenge: put yourself to test with much variety of fun challenges (I consider this as training mode)
-Multi player: non-existent...they lied to us on this part T_T
Pros:
-It's dynasty warriors on the pc
-it has all the DLC's and new added content from the PS3 version
-Lu Bu daughter is hawt!
-AMBITION! Seems to be fleshed out, haven’t played much of this mode but I heard that you can use traps on the battlefield to aid you
-Moral has been reintroduced it this instalment series for people who haven’t played DW8 on PS3. The moral also severely weaken yours or the enemies attacking strength which can turn a losing battle into an outrageous victory
-Did I mention Lu Bu daughter?
-you slaughter 1000s of people per map easily
-Ultimate, prepare to cry some more
Cons:
-I found myself in an infinite loop trying to exit the game, I ended up tabbing out and force closing it.
-If you're use to the PS3 controls, Tip: Musou is now accept and jump is back at the same time
-a big ♥♥♥♥ you by not having a multiplayer option, and I wanted to slaughter more people with my friends
-graphics seems to be subpar, even by PS3 standards in my opinion, I think the PS3 had better quality
-just got all characters to lvl 99 last month on my PS3, and now I have to do it gain T_T
All in all, it was what I expected from a ported game, and as I said, I bought it for future hope. If KOEI can learn from BANDAI NAMCO Games with their Dark Souls and Dark Souls 2, then this can become a very good game on PC with better quality, more zeal and larger battles that will force us to take the entire 60 mins allotted time to complete.

Welcome to 2014, and the 1080p 60fps Dynasty Warrior 8 is officially on the PC platform! Why do I have to start this way? Trust me, resolution and frame rate per seconds is the core issue for a lot of gamers nowadays as they approach new titles. The moment you take your very first move in your very first actual round of the game really is the moment of truth of whether the game turns you up or turns you down. We as the PC gamers don’t like the hidden 30fps lock, or anything like that! NO. Let’s NOT talk about  that anymore since it’s not what we have here.
Gameplay
*** to knock out hundreds and thousands of AI dummies in a single round.***
For the new to the series players, this is an action game where you control a single character in 3rd person mode and mash just a couple of buttons (one button can do it too if you prefer -_-!) to knock out hundreds and thousands of AI dummies in a single round. If you are the causal gamer type just looking for some easy fun, this game is really the chosen one for you. Dynasty Warrior 8 really makes me feel like an overpowered monster in the three kingdom battleground, and I love that very much.
Graphics and Sound
For graphics it is 1080p 60fps, that’s important. However, the style of art in Dynasty Warrior 8 is not that charming in the first impression, feels kind of dull actually.(When do games ever match their graphics with the store page screenshot actually) But the well-made textures in the environment and the detailed face expressions of the characters really brings a smile. That in fact can prove why we can’t judge a game base on first impression of the graphics.
***It’s like watching a Japanese film where a Japanese female screams in her own voice, but suddenly has the American         female voiceover once she starts talking…… WTF. ***
The background music is engaging just to the right point, but the voice acting is kind of weird at some point. What I mean weird is that there are TWO voice actors casting ONE character! The voice that the characters make to respond from getting hit for example, do NOT match up with the voice of the characters in the actual talking dialog. It’s like watching a Japanese film where a Japanese female screams in her own voice, but suddenly has the American female voiceover once she starts talking…… WTF. So I go right ahead and check if there is any option to change the dialog sound into Japanese instead of English. Nope there is none, although that would’ve solve the funny issue, but NOPE. The officials said they will have both the Japanese version and Chinese version released and sold separately in the following of this year. If that’s their marketing strategy of trying to mess with the voice acting and get people to maybe buy their Japanese version of the game as well or anything like that, that’s terrible. I can't say that I despise this game. It just doesn't "do it" for me. I played the first couple of hours on PS3 a few years back on a rental, got bored and returned it, and now I've done the same thing on PC. I only got a few minutes further than I was able to keep interested on PS3 this time around. It's not a terrible game, but if you value certain things in games, you'll be unsatisfied.
For me, I like characters with personality, and this game is pretty devoid of those. I look at something like Vampire The Masquerade Bloodlines, which is
with colorful, memorable characters, then I look at Dragon's Dogma, and even having just played the game, the most stand-out characters aren't of interest to me at all. The game even goes so far as to tell you that your followers aren't even human, or any interesting race. They're just quasi-people who fight just because, and their "personality" consists of a single, generic tone.
One other big thing that I value in a game is a feeling of power. Attacks in this game feel puny, all the way from level 1 to level 7, whether you're fighting a boss or fighting a goblin. Most fights as a warrior consist of blocking when attack, and swinging
times at even the weakest regular enemy until it dies. Bosses are medieval bullet...er...arrow/bolt sponges? As a mage, you wil pew-pew-pew weakly, or even use a longer-casting fire spell that does slightly more damage. The combat is boring enough that I couldn't be bothered to move during a boss fight and won by standing in place for more than half of the battle, just clicking my left mouse button over and over as a mage until the fight ended.
Like I said, the game's not awful or anything, but I do like character personality, and this game is full of bland medieval people, and I like feeling powerful in combat, yet every attack chips away even at wimpy enemies. If those things don't bug you, you might enjoy this game. Most people seem to dig it. I can't recommend it myself, though, as despite to attempts at playing the game, I just can't really say I like it at all.

The major issue cropping up with some players is the cutscenes either lagging heavily or freezing the game entirely. More's the pity since cutscenes are well-animated and abundant. Heard the devteam's aware and working on a patch.
Gameplay for Act: 1 weighs more in exploring the aforementioned charming setting for cheeky humor than puzzle solving. Wouldn't mind half so much if the navigation weren't a little janky, which brings up my only non-bug problem with the game. Hotspots for navigation seem awkwardly placed and unintuitive, making scene-to-scene and scene-to-object a bit clumsy.
With point'n'click, your entire game is the user interface and this one feels like it could use a week of beta testing.

The combat was very lacking in my opinion but I've only fought a few animals and skeletons, I did run into a skeleton boss that almost 2shot me, and I've seen that there's dragons in this game although I've not fought any yet.
Overall, I think that the game could be entertaining for friends to play together once you get over the clunky combat.
For solo play, I think the game can keep you entertained for a couple of hours as I don't know what mid-end game content is like.

What is Mass Effect you might ask well Mass Effect is a Sci-fi action role playing game played through the eyes of Commander Shepard.
Story- The story starts off with the Alliance ship SSV Normandy given a task by the Concil (The Government and sort of like a galactic version of the United Nations.The Concil is lead by three repersentive from races which hold the most territory, miltary might or the most intellectual these these races are the Asari, Turians and the Salarians) to escort a Specte to the human colony called Eden Prime. Bioware fully fleshed out the lore in this universe with all factions have belivable reasons in taking actions even if it's morally wrong for example the Genophage or human prejudices.
Characters- The characters much like the universe are fully fleshed out with them all having their own point of view on topics. Bioware knows how to develop their characters and more the player interacts with them more opportunities will come up such as personal information, character missions and to certain characters they might become your love interest.
Animation and Game Design- Even if the game was release in 2008 the animation does hold up to modern standard with great lighting to enforce the atmosphere where the player might be at the time. The level/ game design from the first game in ways are superior than the sequel. The levels fill much more open and larger than in the second instalment but this might be just something i've noticed.
Conclusion- Before playing this game i didn't really think much about Mass Effect, i thought it was overhyped but i resent my fomer judgement so much. Mass Effect is worth every cent it's worth as well deserves a second time playing through. I 100% recommend this game if you like RPG or games with strong stories.

This game is incredible! I know I've only played for 3 hours so far, but let me tell you how much fun those 3 hours were. Before I start the review, I'd like to acknowledge that the game is only version 0.02 and already amazes me. So the game starts simple; you're in a plane, you go and get a cocktail, and boom, the plane goes down. As you "struggle" to swim out, you find a life raft. As the current sequence ends with an explosion of an engine, you start the actual gameplay. You start floating in the raft with nothing but water and a nearby island to see, and most likely a shark. Once you get to your new home, you need to scavenge for sticks, rocks, and anything else you can find. I also liked the crafting system, it wasn't like "Oh, put this item in a box and it'll magically appear in your inventory", no, it was "throw your items on the ground in a pile and see what you can make of it". So I really liked the crafting system. So after you make your first axe and campfire and chop down some trees, collect some coconuts and crabs, you start to feel bored. But that's fine, the game throws hundreds of explorable islands at you; however, the islands are currently very small and extremely similar, but as the game develops, I'm sure they'll all have differences. When I started playing, I would go to different islands and make basic shelter (basically a pile of sticks, food, and a fire) and just yesterday I made a "map". I figured out North, South, East, and West, and I drew a map of where all the islands were that I discovered in relation to the direction. This is helpful to not get lost. Another fun feature is exploring shipwrecks and other sunken things in the water. In conclusion, I've only played for 3 hours and have not done too much, but the game is very fun so far and I hope to see later on better and bigger (and a variation) different islands and fixed lighting, because one night it was "bright" and realistic, like nights should be, and the other day I played the night was pitch black and impossible to see without fire. So I want to see better islands, improved and ultimitley realistic lighting, and more animals. By animals I don't mean zombies, or pumas or things like that roaming around, but maybe lizards or birds; it just adds to what you can make. And please don't add more guns other than the flare gun, we don't need an impending multiplayer where all people do is make fortresses on a small island and shoot people, that's what Rust is for. And one final thing, I don't want to ever see in this game structures other than buoys, shipwrecks, and islands...I don't want a game where everything is given to you (shelter and items), and also, with what I said about guns, all I would want is a simple, unreliable bow and some arrows made from sticks and rocks. I want to feel like I'm surviving not feel like I'm trapped on an island with nothing but a ton of items to get me through.
EDIT:
This game does get boring after a while...I can't really play for too long before I feel like getting off...not the BEST game, but it's still pretty fun. Maybe if the game was $10 and the creators actually worked on the game more, then it would be a definite buy. But updates are VERY slow and the game gets pretty boring.

At last a survival / horror game that doesn't involve zombies. There are a couple of good 'us against nature' titles, one is the long dark and now stranded deep. Two very different games but with both your worst enemy is mother nature.
With stranded deep you are lost in a procedurally generated ocean populated only by marine life and small islands. You start with just a life dinghy and a couple of items. Starvation and dehydration will kill you quick unless you start taking avantage of the resources on the islands and items found in numerous ship / plane wrecks.
The longest I survived has been 15 + days. Exploration is not without risk as sharks are never far away. This is a very promising survival game in the making. Very playable even at this early stage. My only concern would be that after numerous hours of gameplay whether you would start to get bored. Hopefully the developers will add more content, items to find and challenges to stop this from happening.
The underwater environments are great and no two ship wrecks appear to look the same. Some are just wooden frames while others are more recent large ship wrecks with multiple rooms to explore. Beware though as you can only hold your breath for so long.
8/10 - Would recommend to those too frightened to go on Bear Grylls survival show.

Wow! I backed this game on Kickstarter mostly for the expertise the creators showed. And I'm not disappointed: this is exactly what I whished for - and more! It's Badur's Gate and Icewind Dales on steroids, with a much better class & stat system than D&D, an excellent interface and great graphics. Yes, it uses isometric view and uses a similar art style to the old games, but that's not a bad thing at all. Not everything has to be 3D or First Person to be a good game.
So far, 27h in with my strong hold secured, and half way through the endless paths (but still at the beginning of the main story) I'm really enjoying the world, the story telling and Obsidian's homebrew rpg system. It's so much better than the old D&D adaptions, as they were free to adjust those things they didn't like or that didn't fit to a CRPG, and they were free to develop their own world.
It's a classic fantasy setting, although classes and races differ somewhat. Sure, you find elves and dwarfs, wizards and fighters, but also godlike and ciphers - and front loader pistols and guns. It's got it's own spin on the genre and not for worse. The setting is somewhat gruesome though not black and white. Sure, there are bad guys, but not all are evil - some are just mad from grievance and desperation. It's a great world to explore with a lot of freedom of choice.
If you like good RPGs then this is what you should go for (also try Dininity: Original Sin, another great Kickstarter rpg game, if you haven't already).

Takes the complexity of the Baldur's Gate series and brings it into the modern age.  The work done to the Infinity Engine is absolutely amazing and puts to shame the "enhanced editions" that Beamdog has released for Icewind Dale and Baldur's Gate.

Alright, I know starting a review with that type of header isn't likely to inspire a lot of confidence. But trust me on this one:
This game actually isn't that bad. In fact, it's kind of good?
A.R.E.S. feels straight out of the 90s in both design, story, fidelity, and - let's face it - name. It's an action side-scroller and you control a robot dude. You have access to several types of weapons (that you're never not spamming the entire level), and you use them to mow down hordes of enemies and the occasional boss. There are some RPG-lite elements, like weapon upgrading and new suits, but it's all pretty shallow.
It's short, and not all that hard. Its understanding of level design is...uh...
. It's colorful and full of neon. Did I mention you're constantly firing guns? Like,
?
That's it. That's all there is. But there doesn't need to be anymore, right? This isn't a "fake" retro game, there are no surprise plot twists or usage of ironic "bad design"
In fact, maybe that's why the experience felt so good: it was genuine. It felt like a dumb action game that was perfectly content providing that exact experience - a callback without all the "heh, remember THIS?!" that plagues so many others.
It's a fun game, and I think you'll have fun with it as well.

Their monetization policy on their store page is false.
"Monetization:
Art of War: Red Tides will adopt “free download + in-game purchase” pattern, and the in-game store will sell neither exclusive items that could influence the match, nor in-game currencies."
They actually sell Large crates which hold runes and patterns for units. A whale could get a significant rune advantage if they throw loads of cash at these crates.
The second way is alternative decks/rune pages you can only obtain through the ingame store. You would want these if one or two units is banned in ranked to change your strategy. Bad game a lot of animation/graphic bugs and unbalanced units. The game is pay to win even though it's suppose to be a skill based game. You start off with some basic units and if you want more units you need to unlock them by using in-game currency or real $$. By using real money you can level faster and get more in-game currency while everyone else waits for their weekly currency limit to reset.
Most of the unlocked units are better than the basic ones, you basically can't play terran without HEF flamethrowers unlocked. While unlocking units can be expensive and time consuming, the most p2w part of the game is the rune system. Basically we can play the same amount of time and have the same units but if I put real money into leveling my runes my army will have 5% more damage, 10% more armor, and 4% more health than yours. I can also create a larger army than yours by upgrading my soul essence mine 53% faster with the overseer rune. Basically everyone that's top 10 in the global leadership board got high level runes and played the game for a long time. Skill matters but pay2win can close the gap, and if your both equally skilled then p2win decide who wins.

Great game. While not innovative, it was incredibly refreshing to play a game whose sole purpose was to be fun. It's very streamlined in this sense, and it faciliates the unique nemesis system. This is truly the meat of the game. Essentially it creates unique orcs from a huge pool of traits, and makes them bosses in the world. The traits are fairly varied and the level of detail put into the orcs is astounding. The game has an upgrade system which was actually diverse and I found myself using a lot of the neat abilities you can get. All in all there's definitely a lot of fun to be had here, but there's not a lot to say about it really.
Now there's only a handful of things about this game I could criticize. I found the movie name dropping and general quoting was pretty obvious. While it's good material, it just felt odd. And while the story starts off brilliantly it then becomes erratic and hard to follow due to multiple forces pushing you each way. The last two "bosses" were just quicktime events pretty much, and the last boss would be the huge Graug as far as I consider it. Lastly the nemesis system starts to wear itself thin. Sure the orcs may look new and unique, it's really just a skin on top of the recycled quirks they have.
All in all, I'm hoping for some sort of sequel because this one had a lot of what I liked, but definitely left me wanting more. It is a very satisfying game to be sure, and I can safely say my money and time was not wasted.

If you dont like this game within the first 2 hours you wont like the rest of it. For me it's a refreshing spin on your typical third person RPG. Seems more linear to a fair degree and in a good way. It's refreshing almost.
What I've enjoyed so far:
- The animations are superb. Seriously.
- The movement feels planted, there's a fair amount of climbing and jumping accross rooftops and it just feels so effortless while not feeling like the game is doing all the work for you, feels very connected. Never floaty.
- The armour and weapons look really good considering the age of the game and there's a huge variety.
- The boss fights feel meaty and substantial.
- In fact the combat as a whole feels really flushed out, i think this is largely due to the animations (bare in mind i havent played as a magic caster/user so I cant give a review based on that).
- It's challenging. Not dark souls stupid punishing but the game isnt affraid to give you a good slap across the face if you mess up.
What I havent enjoyed so far:
- The UI is pretty bloody awful, it's very obviously a console port. It's not completely terrible, it's still totally fuctional but i found myself using the arrow keys as oppsed to the mouse more often than not. It just makes inventory management tidious.
- There's a ton of inventory management. You have a party of 4 so you're constantly stopping to organise all the items you've looted.
- The story is probably quite good, i wouldnt really know cos it's delivered terribly.
- Inventory management, clunky UI and, if you have the patience for it, story delivery all contribute to the pacing of the game being pretty off. Feels like you're stopping and starting and personally it's a major turn off.
- Looting is a pain the♥♥♥♥♥ you have to to turn your character to face the item you wish to pick up (console port BS) and cant just turn your camera to look at said item. On top of that the items on the ground only make themselves considerably more obvious by a white light above them when you're very close to them. So imagine killing a mob, running up to it, not being sure if it dropped anything, eventually seeing that yes it did and there's loot next to it's corpse and then having to face your character directly at it to loot it. (lots of that)
-The world feels very static. Almost empty. It's due to a conbination of a lack of ambient noise in cities, a lack of NPCs roaming about and a lack of random encounters.
- You have quite literally no emotional bond with the members of your party. You literally just recruit random NPCs, no back story, nothing. They're just random NPCs that you talk to and say "yup lets hire you" and there's hunders of them just standing around waiting for you to pick them.
- Come to think of it none of the NPCs have any sort of personality. It's not a game you play to roleplay within or to get immersed in the story
Honestly its the combat and animations that carry this game. They're exceptional. Truely. You start the game imidiately in combat so if you dont like it right away, you wont like the game. Which is good cos you can just refund it and not have to worry. So try it out at least.
