The game is very good but here is a list of things that would improve it:

If you like beautiful, realistic graphics with the best dynamic lighting you can get in a game, this one is for you. It runs on cryengine and is the first game to use the SVOGI feature, which seems responsible for ambient occlusion, great shadows and something I haven't seen in other games before: real dynamic indirect lighting. In miscreated when the afternoon sun falls through the windows on an orange pillow e.g., the lit surface will act as an additional light source and cast an orange shine on a close by wall. At a first glance you may not even notice, but when you look at the scene as a whole it really works the magic and transforms a bunch of polygons into an authentic world.
I think the very convincing lighting is one of the central factors why this game is so incredibly immersive. You can have bright daylight, dense fog, rain, thunderstorms, rainbows, you can even go chasing up tornadoes. There are beautiful golden mornings and wonderful sunsets. And, of course, there's the nights, and in this game nights are "real" which means sometimes you can see really well outside (in the moonlight), but brightness varies and it can get pitch black within minutes (probably because of clouds masking the moon).
You will often need your torch in buildings to find loot, in the nighttime facing the inside of a room without a light your monitor may as well be off (C:
But, seeing in the dark in miscreated means being seen as well - you can see player's torches over very long distances, you can check out the airfield or whole streets just by watching from a nearby hill cause players' torches realistically cast their light through the windows on the streets and nearby houses... the reflection of your friend's torch through a window on the first floor on a window of a house across the street may make the hair on the back of your neck stand up regularly.
Water in general and all the weather effects are well done too, with loud wind and deep thunder... the tornadoes look amazing... the water on surfaces when it's raining looks great... when I found a garden gnome (you can put these in your base (C: ) with my torch when it was raining in the dark, I saw a red halo around it from the reflections of the water drops in the air. Running across meadows in fog so dense I could barely see my friend's back was an experience no other game could deliver so far, and in miscreated there are many moments like this. Exploring a cave and seeing your own shadow dance before you in the light of your friend's torch, exchanging fire in the dark on a scaffold opposite the police station in Hayward Valley with chemlights and smoke grenades being thrown...
And it's hardcore realism. No names or health bars above players heads. No crosshairs. No "'M' for map" and you know where you are - you will need to read road sings and look for landmarks until the map sinks in and after maybe 150 hours of gameplay you just "know" where you are when you respawn after ending up on the wrong end of a gun. No compass - follow rivers or the position of the sun. You may give up your position hiding from enemies in a bush when you need to eat or drink because people close-by may hear you gulp.
Depending on the number of players on a server you may be looting without running into other guys for some time... but in my opinion that's exactly what this game is about. If you like to play a fps, go play a fps. I like fps, but they're more like a sport, it's about skills and speed and the goal is usually very clear. Miscreated is different.
When you go from house to house searching for food and better gear (you have to eat and drink regularly and wounds heal faster if you're not starving), a suspension builds up which can get scary as hell... it's a permanent "quiet before the storm", and when you run into other players, the situation can go many ways because the community is very diverse... one evening we ended up in a large group of all-friendly people of different nationalities going to the airfield and getting a truck up and running, another time we went down a hill towards a seemingly abandoned base and were shot at before we could even hear the shots (so far away were the snipers)... we were hit and had dirt on our face (screen) from bullets hitting the ground nearby. We were chased through the woods probably getting insulted in chinese in the area chat (C: other times, people were trying to lure us out: "Hey man I'm starving, come out and I will give you my quad for a can of ravioli..." (C:
There's KOS, there's RP servers, there's some really friendly people, but the general advice is, don't trust anyone... but then again, you may get killed and want revenge and shoot the next guy you run across and then get a really bad conscience because he said something really friendly just before you blew his brains out.
In my experience, this 'culture' varies from server to server so you may try different ones until you get the experience you're looking for. As for player numbers, it's a maximum of 36 players on an 8 by 8 km map, which in my experience means
~ 5 players online:
encounters are rare. You can feel relatively safe looting even hot-spot areas or can work on your base alone.
~ 15:
you may be looting for some time without running into someone, but you can run into a "situation" and kill or be killed within seconds... and in my experience the "heart attack factor" is proportional to the quiet time before (C:
~ 25:
for me just right. you have to be really careful, but you have a chance to find some decent gear before getting killed as a fresh spawn and after that it's a good mixture of action and "pre-action" (C:
~ 35:
on a full server, really go to stealth mode and basically don't breathe until you find some decent weapons and ammo (C:
There are many details I love about this game - when you've been playing for a while you really see the dedication of the developers and the vision they follow. It's a rather small team as far as I know, but they do a great job making the world as real and immersive as possible, and though everything is not yet perfect, there are patches every 3 or 4 weeks and you will notice better performance, better textures or LODs here and there, the accessible part of the map grows and grows (currently around half the island which is already huge, in > 150 hours of gameplay I haven't seen all places), new usable vehicles appear or features like non-hostile animals (pigs and roosters) which you can carry to your base... wolves, deer, squirrels... can't wait for the next patch (C:
The cons - though I love the general graphics and atmosphere, some textures and LOD could be better, but I know they're working on it. Then, within the first few minutes I experience freezes when the game seems to load something, but after that it ususally doesn't happen again. Inventory is still buggy sometimes and sometimes items disappear when you drop them on the ground to trade between players, I hope they fix that very soon because you really don't want to lose a rare weapon that way.
Overall, the game feels very "finished" for an alpha and is totally enjoyable, it's less buggy than some titles from much bigger studios when they came out and I really think it deserves attention, appreciation and a growing player base.
And no, I didn't receive a free copy or stand in any relation to the developers or even get money for it, I just really appreciate the game and I want good and sometimes sadly underrated projects to live. I have 198 games in my Steam library and guess I won't be touching most of them for a while as I'm just starting to "really play" Miscreated.
I paid 10 Euros for the alpha and asked the guys at Entrada Interactive whether I could donate another 40 because I really want to support this and pay for it as a full price game and they told me I should write a review instead because that's what they needed most.
So here it is.

Over all a great story, with amazing music and visuals to boot. The story was simply a master peace, and was very griping and emotional. The plot over all was pritty preditable after the first half, however the VN was not going for some crazy twists. Just a simple love story, that they nailed out of the park. Overall reading this at about a medum pace, I finished in about 6 hours, if you want to power-read (and skip over the great music) you can probably finish in about 4 hours.
Some negative aspects in my option are the amount of game-play was a little short, but that could just be me wanting more of this great story. Another huge negative, this VN has you making no choices, despite the fact their are about 4 "choice options" were the main character chooses for you. It is almost as if the writer wanted a branching story and got in a fight with the director who wanted a linar story. This aspect makes the game have zero replayablaty. 6 hours, you cry, your done. Keep this in mind.
As far as the little extras go, the do have a "memories" section that allow you to look at sceens that you have already cleared, as well as listion to music already played. This section is pritty standed in most VN, what I am sad about is they dont have a screen-shot download (as far as I can tell) for the sceens, which is sad considering the art is pritty high quality. Another disaponting aspect is (as far as I can tell) can't buy the sound track through steam (or anywere really.)

Honestly it's alright. Now, that might be anticlimactic but on the whole The strategic layer is kinda fun - I actually enjoy the need to pick and choose what gets built where and I'm ok with making sacrifices in some regions to allow others to develop, to me it adds some weight to the decision making and kinda feels more realistic. The family tree and the balance between dominion and control is pretty interesting too if somewhat frustrating as the game goes on. The two major things the game does well are the tactical battles and the graphics.
The tactical battles are actually really good this time around, Cavalry is brutal in a charge and ranged units are pretty well balanced. The siege maps are cool if a bit same-y and the amphibious landings are actually pretty awesome. The game looks damn good as well, with the detail in the strategic map something I really enjoy. The procedural damage effects are good too and add something to the city battles. Agents aren't so OP this time around as well, they're useful but not game-endingly powerful despite the AI still using them more than is resonable (if I do say so myself) This game, much like it's predecessors has playable naval battles somewhat akin to those in Shogun 2 and are on the whole not bad, despite the somewhat cheesy tendency for naval troops to be defeated by embarked land forces, although this can be countered by staying at range or using the satisfyingly destructive artillery ships.
The main reason for this negative review is by now a dead horse so furiously beaten that it's probably just mush by now - the pretty awful DLC policy that's also made a rather galling appearance in warhammer - which i've for some reason brought on sale but not really played yet. As someone who's paid up for pretty much all the DLC i'd say that all of it with the possible exception of age of charlemagne  and the empires of the sands all the "culture packs" are just damn reskins with too few unique units and maybe some story content - which is in itself kinda interesting but not worth the price in any real way. This really does feel like half of a game which was then filled in with DLC.
The second issue I have with attilla is the AWFUL optimization - my machine is admittedly not at all impressive but I far surpass the minimum system requirements. Thankfully this issue has been mostly fixed with patches and now the game runs pretty well on the whole - Although I do still get the odd slowdown when things get hectic.
As someone who's never played ROME 1 or 2 I can't say how this Attila stands up next to it's closest bretheren but in my mind it's a decisive step backwards from Shogun II, Medieval II or even Empire. The rumored Total war: Victoria may yet reverse the worrying trend of DLC-centric game presentation but until then i'd recommend The fall of the samurai over the fall of Rome any day. Attila is certainly alright, but you've got any doubts wait until it's on sale and be picky with DLC. The last Roman is just stupid and the blood and burning pack is blatant money grabbing and is simply bloody awful. (sorry)

35 hours..  That's the amount I've time by this point I've put into Attila, in those 35 hours I've played just two of the many factions,  only took but 3 settlements for my own and as of this moment in time not completed a campaign..  So what's it like?
Well it's hard on new comers that's for sure, think of it as a civ game but with a whole lot more depth,  and a fantastic battle system where every unit you have on the battlefield has a role and use,  tactics are key but if like me your terrible when it comes to strategic management and thinking you can beat your enemies with POWER!! AKA numbers.
There are a few problems with Attila though
- The prologue which serves as a tutorial only teaches you the bare minimum needed also it has a tendency to not work as intended towards the end.
- The turn clock is soooo slow!  You can make a brew in the time it takes to get to your next turn. Do far I've found no fix

-For newcomers there's a lot to chew on which can be rather overwhelming,  it took me a months break to get into it,  first time I booted it up I was bewildered to say the least.
With these negatives in mind though there is a silver lining...  The community for the Total War games is fantastic and there's always the help you need if you give the energy to search for what you're stuck with.
That being said I still don't understand certain things and find myself in the rough after taking over more than one settlement.
This really is a fantastic game that just needs a bit of your time. And right now it's on sale..  For 8 bloody quid!! If you like civilization style games at all,  or the idea of building an empire this game will see you right.  If you want to destroy the world..  Same applies.
Just remember those hours you sink into this game you'll never get back!

Isaac and his mother lived alone in a small house on a hill. Isaac kept to himself, drawing pictures, and playing with his toys, as his mom watched christian broadcasts on the television.
Life was simple, and they were both happy. That was until the day Isaac's mom heard a voice from above;
"Your son has become corrupted by sin! He needs to be saved!"
"I will do my best to save him, my lord" his mother replied, Rushing into Isaac's room, removing all that was evil from his life.
Again, the voice called to her; "Isaac's soul is still corrupt! He needs to be cut off from all that is evil in this world, and confess his sins!" "I will follow your instructions lord, I have faith in thee" Isaac's mother replied, as she locked Isaac in his room, away from the evils of the world.
One last time, Isaac's mom heard the voice of god calling to her; "You've done as I've asked, but I still question your devotion to me. To prove your faith, I will ask one more thing of you"
"Yes lord, anything" Isaac's mother begged. "To prove your love and devotion, I require a sacrifice, your son Isaac will be this sacrifice. Go into his room, and end his life as an offering to me to prove you love me above all else"
"Yes lord" she replied, grabbing a butcher's knife from the kitchen.
Isaac, watching through a crack in his door, trembled in fear.
Scrambling around his room to find a hiding place, he noticed a trap door to the basement, hidden under his rug.
Without hesitation, he flung open the hatch, just as his mother burst through his door, and threw himself down, into the unknown depths below.
...
Isaac was cornered. his mother, fueled with the desire to serve her god, was bearing down on Isaac.
"I will do as I'm told, my lord. I love you above all else" Isaac's mother repeated to herself.
This was the end of the line for Isaac, his mother was far too strong for him.
But just as he accepted his fate, god intervened, sending an angel down from above to stop his mother's hand.
And just like that, it was over.

What is essentially a StarCraft user map turned into its own game. Art of War takes a classic and unique game mode and attempts to turn it into a full-fledged game. The classic game mode in its original iterations comes across as a great way to kill some time while remaining deceptively deep and addictive. Game play mechanics that are simple on their surface but reveals deeper strategy as the player learns about brute strategies and counter play. These dynamic and adaptive mechanics that begin to surface as the player puts forth the time and effort define the Art of War gameplay.
The game is Free2Play. Those who worry the game is Pay2Win should not be. Pay2Skin is here, being able to cosmetic up your units is a great way to make the battlefield look fresh, as well as the developers new found map changes that differentiate the maps through unique map specific NPC bosses. The player does have the option to purchase around much of the grind for units and runes, but the effectiveness of runes is negligible, especially when you consider the amount of money that would be needed to buy your way into higher tiers. Not to mention this does nothing to effect relative gameplay. Like I said earlier, units have their own unique advantages but counter play is at the crux of the core mechanics.
Pros-
•	Fun gameplay, adaptive strategies, feels like you could never have a perfect build as skill plays heavily into performance.
•	Different races that come with their own unique units, makes each feel distinct and useful.
•	Possibility for growth. The game has much ahead of it, with new maps and units, maybe even another race launch. This game has much life ahead of it.
Cons-
•	Some units don’t seem to perform their function very well. Some races just don’t have effective responses for some units of other races. Also, the difference between early and late game units drastically varies. Some early game units remain relative even in the late game while some late game units will feel useless against some early game units. Scaling unit stats needs to feel more appropriate.
•	Some stats, like armor specifically, are not well communicated to the players in terms of how they work or mitigate damage.
•	Many of the units have useless or pointless upgrades, perhaps fixed by a tree of options, spanning from offense power boosts/ defense stat boosts/ or utility boosts instead of a fixed and limited tree.
•	Unit AI could use some improvements. Units will often target, unnecessarily, other units that would often be killed otherwise to other attacks. This causes units to bunch up and ‘overkill’ another unit and leaves themselves vulnerable. Another issue would be the obvious lag between switching targets and the slow movement many units have right after they attack, causing them to ‘limp’ to another target, often ‘limping’ between targets because of target lag and unnecessary bunching together on single targets. (most notably effects melee units)
•	The game has a weird mechanic often associated with mobile games, that diminishes progress if you play over a certain amount each week. This mechanic doesn’t fit the game well as progress is already slow and incremental, not to mention the negligible benefit of having unlocked more things then a newer player.
Overall, Art of War is moving in a great direction. They could use more units and maps, maybe even races. They could do with some tweaking of current game stats and general balance as well as improvements to the AI, but these are things often associated with simple progress over time by the developer. Games that have been out for years, like popular MOBAs are still doing these same things even after years. It would be appropriate for me then to say that Art of War is in a perfectly playable and agreeable state, and has much life ahead of it.

Heck, I was almost sure I had already wrote a review about Bastion!
Anyways, I came to Bastion - SuperGiant's first game - only after discovering Transistor, which is the second one made by that studio and to me by far the best one, even compared to their third effort (Pyre).
Bastion is anyways, simply awesome.
Its graphics are amazing, and the world - every single level, literally - unfolds ahead of your eyes while you're walking.
The narration is great, just like in Transistor and Pyre, and it guides you thorougly through your epic journey in rebuilding the Bastion - your "core" in which you can build step by step, unlock and upgrade new places (weapons/forge shop, temples with idols, sidequest scoreboards, a distillery.. you can upgrade everything too!).
The game itself is a pure action RPG, in which you have two weapons of your choice and a special attack; it's playable on keyboards too, but it has a perfect joypad support. Maybe, a negative thing is that if you find yourself good with two weapons you're not that pushed into trying the whole of them, something that you constantly do in Transistor (and they did a great upgrade in this field).. I found some weapons really better than others and so the majority of them I used only for the special trials and nothing more. But it's really ok, all in all action RPGs often have only a melee attack xD
The soundtrack is amazing, like the artwork. Nothing else to say, it's all greatly mixed together and you never have the feeling that something is out of place.
The other negative point can be a repetitivity in the gameplay, since the levels are all quite the same and they don't require some special strategies; Bastion's main point is of course not replayability, although I played it for two full times and have been really satisfied with that. But this can vary from player to player; anyways, to me, the enemies in the later stages of the game tend to be copies of the previous ones and the mechanics are very good but as I said with weapons, if you've found your own game style you're driven more to enforce and empower your own style rather than try different strategies - things that you must do in the other Supergiant games.
Reviews that get like 600 likes say that the replayability is awesome due to the fact that they spent 25 hours in the game. For me, it's good when you spend at least 70 or 80 hours in and for an RPG but yeah it's personal xD
Since this is the first game of this company, anyways, all the more reason to praise the effort - everything is really at its right place and nothing has been left out for randomness or chaos. It's what I call a -complete- game in every detail!
I think that even if you're like me way more towards turn-based (J)RPGs, this is a title that you cannot miss :)
P.S. as always, if you're not an English speaker like me, stick with English - trust me xD

If you liked any single player RPG ever (especially the Baldur's Gate series), buy this game.
There's plenty of tactical crunch in the party-based, realtime-with-pause combat system, but the rules engine is very different to the 2e D&D system the infinity engine games were based on. It'll take some investment to learn how to build effective characters, build a party which is more than the sum of its parts, and dominate in battle. If you're like me, figuring out how all those little opportunities and tradeoffs mesh together is immensely satisfying.
The content itself is dark, richly detailed and inventive enough that conversation and exploration is enjoyable; many of the books you come across in-game are entertaining in their own right. Tired and familiar fantasy tropes are refreshingly absent, and in their stead is a carefully crafted world which feels like a lot like a reimagined, magical, yet grimly historical Europe.
Be prepared to do some research on the forums to work out how to capitalize on your options and figure out the combat system.

I was first introduced to this game in my trusty XBOX 360 when it was first released some months ago. The gameplay during that time was amazing; the zombies were a threat but could be manageable if you used your wits and administered your resources well, the story was simple but it was gradually introducing more features and more difficulty. It was more than okay for an XBOX Live Arcade game, certainly more than I expected from it.
However, after logging over 50 hours on it, I grew tired of it. I needed it refreshed. The game graphics on the console were bad; the framerate was terrible; and I thought to myself: this game has been designed for the wrong platform. It should have been designed for PC.
And then, out of the blue, Undead Labs said: "Hey! We know you wanted the game to have better graphics, and an increasing difficulty mode without the story lowering it for you. So here's the Steam release. And have yourself the Sandbox mode DLC too. We know you want it."
And I certainly did. And the graphics were really, REALLY better than their console counterparts. And the implemented keyboard and mouse controls felt so comfortable I really couldn't believe this game had been designed for controllers.
So, my fellow survivor, if you're into the whole zombie apocalypse thing and want a game about surviving at its finest, then this is the game for you. No more gathering useless stuff to be killed by a camper in The War Z or Day Z. No more linear story zombie massacre from Left 4 Dead and Contagion. No more top-down objective scenarios from Shadowgrounds: Survivors. No more sidescrolling platform action from Deadlight.
THIS is the ultimate zombie survival game you've been waiting for. Building your own base. Managing your own community. Playing with several characters. Permanent death for each character, thus bringing more realism. No more useless looting; everything you get is a resource you can develop into something useful in your base. No more passive gaming; your characters may and will get sick, or get hurt, or suffer from starvation. And finally, no more cash-milking developers: Undead Labs brings patches on a regular basis, and actually listens to the community.
All in all, and considering this is their first attempt into this, they did a pretty damn right job. All I'm doing right now is playing this on the refurbished PC version and asking myself: WHERE IS CLASS 4!? WHERE IS STATE OF DECAY 2!?
I hope it's here soon and it brings a new engine, more realistic and better looking. Because State of Decay is one of the few games out there that deserves that.

The survival and limited resources aspect has been what keeps dragging me back. There's buildings to check for supplies, resources to gather, infections and hordes to clear... the map isn't big, but, so far, it doesn't seem to end. Some things on your home base can happen while you are not playing the game, too. None of the characters can die while you're not playing, though!
There are some quirks that are probably related to being a pc port and perhaps will end up being fixed. The big one that gets me is random lag spikes, most often while driving. It's not game-ruining, though it has brought me into a couple close calls.

You can craft a small crappy shack without using too many resources from the island, but each island is quite small and if you have a grand vision for your shack, you'll definitely have to travel to the different randomized islands surrounding yours-- you definitely will need to when your supply of food runs out. Each island has a chance to spawn with a boat wreckage near it, which will have valuable supplies inside.
My least favorite part of the game is traveling between islands, as it takes probably 3 or 4 minutes of constantly paddling your raft to get to the closest island. Eventually you are able to find parts and craft a boat motor that will make travel much faster, but it can get dicey keeping track of where your home base is as you hop around the map.
I have a feeling that the crafting system is in it's infancy and later on there will be more things you can discover and craft. Hopefully. 7/10

Just finished reading this, and those darn onion ninjas have broken into my house again.
This is a kinetic novel, not a game -- there are no choices and no way to alter the story -- but the story it does tell is masterfully written.  And masterfully animated, too -- while other than a brief intro movie there are no FMVs, there are still lots of changes to the backgrounds and sprites, and something that AFAIK is unique to this story (though I'd love to see more of): fully animated lip movements to go with fully voiced characters.
While the ending itself is pretty obvious from early on, it's still a wonderful ride to get there, and the way it plays out simply surpasses all expectations.

It's very rarely I stay up until past midnight to beat a game, let alone Visual Novel. This game just did it.
eden is a kinetic visual novel with almost no required input whatsoever from the players, as the game naturally flows by itself. No branching story, no multiple endings etc. Be it so, it is brilliant on its own. The characters, the story, the soundtrack, all fit together.
Many people say the artwork or graphic is stunning. It is true. There's a real art involved in this game. While it's just a mere 2D pictures, the backgrounds of each frames are nicely put together and designed, smooth flows between the transitions. The characters arts are what you can expect from Japanese games, pretty. Moreover, there's a nice design like characters eyes' blink and their expression changes, lips move in sync accordingly when the mood changes/talks. Simple touch, but meaningful - it makes everything as a whole more lively. Although yes, I do have one complaint, that is - the eyes of those chars are a bit too big overall, makes it a bit weird.
Don't forget the important part for Visual Novel - it's the voice acting. While bunch of VNs abandon the voice acting because of many reasons, eden doesn't neglect it. The voice acting here is simply too good and unquestionably high production value. The actors really really pushed themselves to the limit, the emotions they bring through sheer voice acting alone is too incredible whether they portray happiness or sadness, they do it correctly. Can't deny this one is probably the strongest element this game has. That said, I'd recommend you let the game plays for you, so you get the fullest experience from hearing the voice acting. Voice acting is done in Japanese while the subtitle is in English. As someone who watches a lot of anime, I really appreciate it.
Then there's a mixing element of VN, story. The story starts out slowly and seemingly simple - our protagonist Ryou is assigned to protect military base and the female protagonist Sion. But as the game progresses things getting more intense - until the first act in Military Base ends -, and the last half of the game where Ryou and Sion away, it starts slowing down again. You'll mostly see development of Ryou and Sion's relationship, how two humans with very different background fall for each others. Sad moment, happy moment, funny moment, sad again rinse and repeat. Roller coaster storyline, but by no means bad. In fact, it's very well written when combined with the game arts and voice acting. Can't say much without spoiling, and it's not funny to spoil people's experience on VN game, isn't it? Do note, again, this is a Kinetic VN. There's only one ending as an end result of one linear story and despite you know the ending is coming as you imagine and you don't want it to come, you can't stop playing.
(....even I shed a tear or two watching the ending...)
Now there's a con. The game's performance is a bit bad. It does not support controller natively, and this is an annoyance for people who love to lay down comfortably on the bed while reading the texts. There's also a major problem with Steam Overlay (the Developer admitted it already, and can't fix it with their current resources) so people might have problem taking a screenshot or two. I also had a problem launching the game, not until I complained endlessly and had the Developer fixed it with beta branch which I'm currently using.
I also have to mention that the OSTs are not included in this Steam, be it within the game files so you can listen to them using Winamp for example, or being sold as DLCs. Too bad, would love to grab 'em - the soundtracks are really good. Here's one full song for opening movie from Youtube:
eden is about ten hours long if you keep playing like my pace - letting the game does everything by itself.
VN is a genre that's not too popular on Steam, but overall, eden is a worthy game for any VN fans.
9/10

It took me a long time to get around to playing through this game. Partly because my backlog these days is so massive that it is more than a little overwhelming, and partly because I had a sense this game would probably make me sad. Turns out both of these are true, particularly the latter. ;_;
But... it's a nice little story. A bit predictable perhaps in that you can guess how it is going to end hours before it does, but not everything needs to surprise or shock. Also this is a "kinetic" novel, so there are no choices to make. Just read the text, listen to the voices, and look at the artwork.
Good thing that all of those things are generally well-done. The art in particular stands out. The amount of CG's is staggering, the "regular" artwork looks just as good, and they even gave some attention to male characters here (unlike alot of other VN's XD). The voice acting works alright, and I was amused to find out that the male lead in this is voiced by someone who has voiced another male lead in one of the few romance VN's/animes that i've actually seen (Takasu Ryuuji from Toradora!). Lastly, I don't recall any parts of the text that seemed badly worded or mistranslated, so hooray for that.
The cast is fairly small, but they are interesting even if most of their backstories involve something they regret or wish for. The male lead Ryou starts off as a cynical emotionally dead soldier who has seen far too much violence and lost sight of what he is truly living for. The female lead Sion, despite looking like a loli and being
older than she looks, is a lonely high-functioning autistic who is a victim of her own genius and unable to really enjoy her life (sounds familiar ;_;). The rest of the cast, from the seemingly bubbly Lavie, the actually bubbly Maya, the caring big-sister figure Elica, and the regretful Major Inaba all play their parts in the story, but, since this is a romance, ultimately eden* is dominated by Ryou and Sion. As for them working as a couple... I've seen better, but I've also seen much worse. It's fine.
So it's a relatively short (<10 hours) KN with superb art and decent story/characters. Also being a VN with a serious and emotional plot without any fan service nonsense is always welcome to see on Steam. I liked it, don't regret playing it, and that's good enough for me. :3

This is not really a video game. This is a kinetic novel, a visual novel that plays without any player decisions. It compares more with a novel or a movie, so those looking for anything resembling 99% of video games should look elsewhere, but those who are looking for an excellent story may look no further.
As a game that is entirely based upon story, eden* delivers.
eden* is a character-driven experience. Plot twists are used sparingly, and the story flows about as how you would expect. It is in the characters that the game shines. None of them resemble any cookie-cutter archetypes, especially those commonly found in anime or other visual novels. They feel human. They have a million different things on their mind, and the emotions attached to them are incredibly complex, and the game isn't afraid of discussing those conflicts inside each of those characters. It is especially apparent with the two lead characters' interactions; they understand each other's complexities almost absurdly well. It's a great joy seeing them change in even some minute ways as they face the very end.
The orchestral soundtrack is excellent and accents the story very well. The visuals are refreshingly more dynamic than most other visual novels, showing scenes from "camera angles" beyond the usual cut-and-paste sprite approach. Hearing different voices in different ears depending on the placement of the "camera" is a nice touch if you wear headphones.
As for downsides, the game is a little short. My record is a little bloated from semi-frequent breaks and waiting to hear all of the voice acting before continuing. The story was sweet enough that I didn't care.
The pacing might be a little slow in the beginning. The game definitely takes its time introducing the characters' quirks and histories. Again, eden* is a character-driven experience, so I didn't mind since that's partly why the characters felt so complex.
Finishing the game made me want more, yet the feeling of closure to the character's inner struggles also made me feel satisfied. Loved it from beginning to end.

Well im not sure how to start this since this is my first review of the game. I purchased this game prolly about a year ago with a few of my friends the game was fun and hard, like just finding enough food to stay alive hard. but it was very early in the games career. we played for a bit and then for whatever reason we stopped playing.
Last night we were having a hard time firguring out what game we wanted to play and came back accross this game and were curious to see how things have progressed. took us a few minutes to recapture our bearings on how the game works and before you can make your first bags and boxes inventory management is huge.
Day 1: We run around franticly trying to figure out how to build a shelter and such and start to realize we are not going to get one done before night falls. Night hits and we are huddled around a campfire trying not to freeze to death. get warm enough and tired of staying put so i figure i will go get some more stone to work on things. walk towards a rock and i hear them before i notice them. It's a pack of wolves, so i quickly retreat to the fire hoping like real wild animals they will want to stay away from the campfire. we also manage to encounter a few skelletons which we just dodge the easily choreographed moves and club them down.
Day 2: notice something about making some bigger bags, so i spend the day chasing down and clubbing boars for food and supplies. wandering around the woods i hear wierd noises i attribute to the pigs. Then i hear the flapping and realize as the trees around me burst into flame that it was not a simple boar after all. Panic sets in as i glance up at the sky trying to see what the heck is trying to burn me to a crisp. so i start running inbetween trees and rocks hoping to lose him. after what i assume to be a few more strafing runs looking for me he must have left cause the sounds vanished.
Day 3: By now we have got some decent supplies gathered and have learned how to fight the various beasts in the area: Boars, Wolves and Skeletons. We find a ruined town of sorts with a glowing red skeleton in the center of it. decide we are going to see what hes made of. i go in first to see if i can figure out his attack patter without being murdered. He lunges at me, I sidestep in what i feel is just in time and give him a smack with my stone sword and notice his heath bar barely moves. At that moment we knew we were in for a long fight of hit and run tactics. After what felt like was about 10 minutes we brought him down. Soon after we are making our way back to our base and i hear it again. this time the dragon has now set its sights on my friend. he uses a giant boulder to dodge the dragons 3 strafing runs before the beast appears to have lost interest with him and left.
That was our couple day experience in the game, needless to say we are going to be making another trip into the Savage Lands to see what other adventures we have in store.
Pros:
Dangerous enemies.
While some of the moves they have are somewhat easy to dodge. that one time you don't you will pay for it.
I have read some of the other reviews complaining about the dragon, as long as you stay out of the open and away from his tower he appears to leave you alone for the most part. but just that fear that settles in when hes coming after you is worth it every time.
Fairly In depth crafting system:
Me and my friend have only appeared to scratch the surface of it, but so far so good
Sense of Survival:
From the aspect of staying warm to starving to death, you do get that feeling like there is more than just monsters that threaten your life.
No gamebreaking bugs so far:
Yeah no bugs we have found so far have made the game unplayable.
Cons:
Sharp learning curve:
not sure if its a pro or a con, but the game is a little overwhelming at first if you are not very accustomed to survival games.
Not sure how well this game works solo:
As i stated i played this game with a friend, i can see the world and lack of inventory room at the begining very harsh for someone playing by themselves.
Conclusion:
Thumbs up!
It has enough going good for me to reccomend this game to others with what ive seen. It also has enough different with it to justify getting it with the large amount of survival games on the market at the moment. I would buy this game again just for the few experiences i have had with it. I look forward to seeing whats coming next from the devs. they seem to update this game pretty frequently.

PoE is set in the world of Eora, a world of magic, swords and early gunpowder weaponry. The setting presents a fresh and uniquely rich experience which is reminiscent of my first exposure to the D&D forgotten realms universe. It is clear that PoE takes inspiration from earlier CRPGs such as Baldurs Gate and Planescape Torment, even emulating the graphical style of the time, however it is not a simple boilerplate reproduction.
PoE manages to capture the storytelling finesse of its spiritual predecessors, but modernises it with significant improvements to gameplay. Hit points are handled with a new two tier system, consisting of endurance which defines how much damage you can sustain in a single encounter and which recovers at the end of combat, and health which is a larger pool and represents your closeness to death. Rest in the wilderness is also limited through the requirement of camping supplies, of which you can only carry 4 at a time. Likewise, abilities are also limited on a per encounter or per rest basis. These changes together result in a much more fluid gaming experience than its predecessors, but at the same time demand a thoughtful approach to the use of resources.
In my opinion, Pillars has filled a CRPG niche that has been left empty since the last of the Infinity engine games and has raised the bar for the genre. If you enjoyed Baldurs Gate or just want a detailed party-based CRPG in a rich setting, you owe it to yourself to play this. I can't recommend it highly enough.
Pros:
* Detailed and engrossing writing.
* A near perfect rule system gives a good degree of challenge and eliminates a number of 'cheap' tactics that were prevealent in D&D era games.
* Strong emphasis on role-playing elements.
* Plenty of opportunities to play to the strengths of your character, whether through character specific dialogue options or alternate solutions to problems.
Cons:
* Damage reduction on creature types seem arbitrary and vary wildly between related creatures.
* 2D graphics won't suit everyone's taste.
* You're still going to need to save your game religiously.

To begin I would like to say I am having tremendous amounts of fun with Miscreated despite the alpha status bugs and glitches, which for me, have been few and far between.
Miscreated is a game set in the year 2089. The Final War has come to an end. The devastation of the war itself is what ended it. If you are un-mutated and alive all you are doing is striving to STAY that way. Mutants roam the once lovely streets. The world is decaying. Focused on scavenging, staying alive, and upping your arsenal and equipment itself is a challenge in itself. Not only are you competing with other survivors for resources, you must be wary of the mutated citizens and areas of the world that remain radiated.
PROS: -Constant anxiety. (Can also be a CON for some)
-Death COULD be around literally any corner. (Can also be a CON for some)
-In game VOIP is smooth and consistent. (Can also be a CON because ANYONE in range will hear you, including those who wish you blow your brains out and steal your gear.)
-Beautiful graphics and lighting system.
-Scavenging is difficult and equally rewarding so it has a very nice feeling of accomplishment.
-Creativity in player interactions is very common in an almost RP way.
-Gravity system exists.. better lead your shots with any long range combat!
-Unexpected friendships/companionship to survive in the wasteland.
-You have the ability to look like a total ♥♥♥♥ing badass.
CONS: -Constant anxiety. (Could be a PRO for some)
-Death COULD be around literally any corner. (Can also be a PRO for some)
-Difficulties in establishing your location in the world when you die and must respawn.
-No character customizable abilities. (YET) So everyones base model is the exact same.
-Some spawn locations for certain items make ZERO sense. EX. A cars drive belt in a refrigerator.
-Housing interiors are just a variation of several layouts copy and pasted. I find myself checking the same homes twice because HEY THEY ALL LOOK THE SAME.
It's slowly but surely getting better.

The game itself is a straightforward point-and-click adventure with a wealth of in-game descriptions. The game consists of solving some puzzles which vary from small games to just clicking on things until you find what you need (that's simplifying it but you really can't miss anything). The descriptions are entertaining, the author put effort into making everything you read worthwhile. The descriptions, as the other reviews can tell you, consist of mostly 90s nostalgia.
The music is relaxing, old-school in terms of flash games (I think), and "nice" overall. The chapter only lasted me ~2 hours and I searched through everything (only got half the achievements so there are hidden interactions throughout). For $7.99, I think it was worth my time but for others it may end rather abrubtly.

It isn't a bad game... but it really needs some polishing. The problems aren't things that will absolutely ruin the game but they will be irritating and annoying over time. To start off, when I click "Quick join" I don't want to be able to join games that are full or in progress. The only servers to be available for quick joining should be ones that haven't started yet and have space. Also, when I click quit, instead of just closing the game, the game stops working. As in, it brings up a tab saying that it's stopped working and it's looking for a solution. Thirdly, weapons will sometimes not work quite how they should. For example, today, I fired quicksand straight at a tank and it just disappeared off the map. From my previous experiences, quicksand is one of the weapons that is actually supposed to impact, not go into the ground like a tunneler or sub-sniper. Finally, some of the missions are really harder or easier than they should be at that point. For example, assistant regional manager took one try while some of the target ones take several days of effort. Overall, I can't say it's a bad game. However, there are issues that make the game annoying to play when they happen.
EDIT: Ignore what I said about the quicksand thing. I was wrong there. The "stopped working" thing also never happens to me anymore. The quick joining is still an issue though. Still also a great game.

collect 20 iron bars to make full armor set, complete a mission, collect 20 tungsten bars to make a set, scan floran objects, complete a mission,collect 20 durasteel bars to make a set, scan hylotl objects, complete a mission,  collect some kind of bar to make a set, scan avian objects...
That is most likelly the main quest in the game, without counting that everytime you start a new character, you are forced to see the same story from Esther.
Exploring the worlds in the game are still quite vague, because most likelly, unless you are looking for ingredients dropped from certain monsters or ores to make a set, or crafting, you will see yourself running from left to right, or from right to left of each world you visit, looking for dungeons or towns, for at least a few percentage of chance of getting a better equipment than the one you are using. After exploring for some time, you'll feel the necessity of buying a hoverbike, because you will grow tired of the same enemies over and over, and the same unrewarding exploration.
The good point, is that now guards no longer nags you to sheathe your weapon, but you still have to beware not to attack a citizen or guard by accident, since that Guard does not know how to arrest you, neither how to "forgive and forget".
Also counting that if the guard is chasing you, other guards in the way of that guard chasing you may also have the death wish the other guard had, which means that you surelly are in problems, and the only way of resolving the situation would be killing the guards.
Also talking about towns, towns now offer you unique items for sale, being that finding an Avian shopping village will be very nice, if you like to buy things, since their variated inventory will most likelly have all items of a set you may get interested into completting, the bad, is that the merchants are complete morons, they usually leave their shops, so you need to find the owner of the store so he can move to his stall, the problem is that once the shop owner reaches his shop, they may decide to idle away just after they reached it, meaning you have to catch them again, and then click them asap once they reach the shop.
Also, It is very unusual for a shopkeeper to leave his store hanging around while waiting for costumers, which makes things not be very much... Realistic.
Other point that were added in the game, also includding towns, is that npcs can occasionally give you quests, which you can complete to gain loot bags, which can come weapons, armors, useable items and upgrade items, beside the quests sometimes can be quite a chore, they sure are quite rewarding, aswell as you can end up having the npc as a recruit for your ship's crew, and you get quests where new merchants appears on the map with their unique items, aswell as rescued npcs moving to the town, making it bigger in population, which is also awesome, the problems with it actually, is that it is very easy for you to accidentally abandon a quest, the other problem is, I'm not sure if anyone else have this issue, but when it comes to a quest of defeating a named bandit, the bandit, beside having an absurd defense, it can also 2 or 3 hit kill your character, making the quest demi impossible for you to complete with the planet's tier equipment, unless you make a box around them with some tile, and fill the box with lava to kill them and complete the quest, but the bad of using that method is that a recruitable bandit may not be able to be recruited to the ship due to that.
Another thing that were implemented into Starbound, is the possibility of creating your own village, yay!!!
You can create your own town with your own houses, furnish them, and then a tenant will spawn based on the
kind of furnitures in your town, sounds awesome, isn't? But it is! The tenants of your town can even give you quests,
Even mod races that have it's own kind of furnitures setup in their house, can be spawned.

wiki for what kind of furnitures are of x type, because the game itself will not tell you, and if you get a quest to spawn
a certain tenant by using that x type furniture, you will also look in the web, unless you use the Colony deed of the quest
giver, then send a huge **** to the quest giver and cancel the quest.
And now, the Crew, your very own ship crew, they can be recruited by spending some time doing quests at the towns, or in your own colony, each crew member have it's own class, which will prove certain benefit in combat or in the ship, unless it's a janitor. They seems to be more durable than your character, plus can be proved to be of good aid to you during your quest in the galaxy, that if they weren't dumb.
I'm not saying that they will be a complete burden to you, but they will not try to avoid traps, and neither leave a lava or poison spot they have fallen into, being that you have either to run away from near the crew member to make him leave that spot either by moving or teleporting, another problem, is that once they are defeated, you must go to your spaceship, and then call them back to the team, since they seems to not know the way back to you, which is annoying, even more when you are deep underground, and it were annoying to reach where you are at.

To go ahead and get it out of the way, I have finished reading this VN completey with the exception of some additional non-canon scenes that are accessible on the non-Steam version and only when the story has been completed, but I will elaborate on that later.
Having read the raving reviews on this story, I decided to give it a try. After all I enjoy stories with substance and content that can be emotionally provocative, which, if you were to read the reviews, eden is just that.
Except it isn't.
Unlikeable characters:
Main character is a stereotypical Gary Stu war-hardened soldier whose inner dialogue takes up at least 60% of the reading which usually wouldn't be a bad thing if it wasn't for the fact that the subject matter of the inner dialogue is always about how emotionless he is. There is hardly any character development, so this doesn't change much. He isn't a good person, not even in a Byronic hero sort of way, and acts like a sociopath, yet still people like him. Okay.
Other main character, Sion, is the typical 100+ year-old "woman" trapped in the body of a prepubescent girl with no personality. That's really all there is to her.
Even when these characters finally show some semblance of emotion, it doesn't provoke any empathy because their backstories are shallow and their characters have hardly been fleshed out at all.
The rest of the characters are either similarly of little depth or are entirely shoehorned in, possibly for the sake of offering some temporary distraction from the otherwise boring plot that seems to drag on forever. By the time any action scenes do occur, you're already numb to what's happening after laboriously clicking/scrolling through the boring "muh stoicism" thoughts of the main character.
The animation isn't bad and neither is the music, although I found it to be noticeably repetitive at times.
At the end of the story, the non-canon, 18+ Plus Mosiac content is unlocked. Not expecting much I decided to open it because I was curious. Surely they wouldn't make the pacing of the non-canon 18+ scenes as mind-numbing as the main story. Nope. It too dragged on for so long I gave up and closed the window before anything involving hentai/18+ happened.

I've played all the total war games sense the original Shogun and I love this one. Wasn't so impressed with Rome 2 and I think Atilla fixed a lot of the issues for me. AI and diplomacy got waaaaay better, and the victory conditions weren't such a massive undertakings either. True to the time period, the campaign is pretty chaotic in a good way. With the Huns destroying everything, you never know what's going to happen and factions get up and migrate all over the map.
What pleases me the most is how fair it is. The original Barbarian Invasion expansion for Rome was pretty bad about the other factions being overpowered with huge armies poping out of thin air when they turn into a horde. In Atilla, if you kill them all in their last city, they're dead. If they had an amry roaming around, that army stays that way and doesn't inflate for no reason. If the AI builds an army too big to support, it shows and they suffer from having no money. The cheating AI and gang up the winner stuff is all gone. I think it's the most fair Total War game I've played so far.
My only complaint is that a lot of the units are the same between factions. Not that big of a deal, but some more cultural diversity would be nice. It's been quite a while since an RPG has kept me THIS HOOKED for the duration of the game. Mass Effect is one of the greats when it comes to Action RPGs (or ARPGs, if anyone calles it that).
Pros:
+ Fantastic story and writing that truly drags you in and doesn't let go
+ Wide array of characters, and they are all deep and interesting
+ Incredible voice acting, with people like Seth Green and Keith Davis having voices
+ Loads of different ways to play, different builds and squads to pick, and a deep upgrade and weapon system
+ Massive amounts of replayability
+ Huge world with tonnes of optional quests
+ Music fits well with the theme, and is well made
+ Quite long. I clocked in at around 15 hours, but I didn't do alot of the side quests. With all the optional content, I would say the game is about 25-30 hours long
Cons:
- The game has a little bit too much customizability, if you can understand that. It can literally take minutes to change all the gear and equipment, and it should have been simplified just a little bit to make it snappier and more enjoyable. It's not that it's hard to understand, you just waste a lot of time on it
- Dialog options are sometimes not entirely clear on what you character will actually say, in what tone he will say it in, if he's being sarcastic ETC. Can lead to some unintentional speech that can affect your relationships on the Normandy
- Optimization is a little wonky, and you can expect some sudden frame drops here and there
Overall rating: 8.5/10 A must play for RPG fans!

===== Full review below =====

The world was destroyed by some fenomenom called the calamity, you're 'the kid' one the few survivors who is trying to restore The Bastion in hopes of make the world take a turn for the better



Bastion's world is composed of several areas which can be accesed via a fast travel map from your base. These areas can be categorized into 3 types:
- Safe Area (The bastion): After the intro level you start up here, this is your operation base.
- Plot Areas: The stages of bastion. You need to clear them to unlock other areas.
- Challenge Areas:  Optional stages which test your skill with a specific weapon. You get up to 3 rewards depending on how well you perform them.
Plot and Challenge areas get locked after you clear them.
As the story progresses, you can access gauntlet areas in The Bastion. Here you fight waves of enemies to know the backstory of the characters and some exp and fragments(game currency).

Bastion is an isometric action rpg. You have a health bar, a potion counter and a tonic counter. Potions heals you and tonics are required to use your special skill. Both can drop from enemies or be recharged on certain buildings inside the stages (fountains or marshal huts which also allow you to switch weapons mid-stage).
There's a variety of
ranged and melee weapons from which you can carry a max of two into combat, each weapon gets a button assigned so no need to swap. As you advance in the game you get different special skills
some specific for the weapons you're carrying, they have no cooldowns but you need tonics to use them.

As defensive maneuvers you can roll and block with your shield. Rolling is a mean to gain distance or dodge telegraphed attacks, you can't attack while rolling.
Blocking with your shield stuns melee enemies and deflects projectiles, you can counter and reflect damage if you a well timed block. What you block depends of the direction your shield is facing. The block button works serves also locks on your angle to face the nearest enemy to you at the moment you pressed it. Lifting your shield slows down.
Bastions combat revolves around kiting groups of enemies until your positioning doesn't get you punished for going melee, timely countering and blocking with the shield and using your sole combat skill to get out of sticky situations. While it sounds simple, the way you do it varies greatly depending on your weapon and skill choice, each enemy has different ways of attacking so the timings for proper countering vary and some simply can't be countered at all so you're required a decent degree of versatility to handle combat situations.

In The Bastion there are buildings, their purpose is letting you access specific menus:
-Distillery: As you level up you can equip beverages which provide bonuses to the kid (lifesteal, more powerful blocking, extra lives, etc). here you select which of these bonuses you want to equip.
-Forge: Here you improve your weapons, you unlock bonuses tiers for your weapons with materials and fragments. Pick one bonus per tier (you can change the selected ones for free anytime) to customize them to your prefered playstyle.
-Arsenal:  Select which two weapons and skill you will carry into combat.
-Memorial: Challenge list, complete them and you will get fragments as rewards.
-Shrine:  Activate or deactivate idols, each idol makes the game harder.
-Lost-and-found: The game's store, buy materials, weapon skill, liquors or idols for the other buildings or mementos to reveal part of bastion's story.
There's a "no sweat" mode which seems to be a easy mode for the sake of just enjoying the story and  normal mode which is the one I will be talking about below.
Activating idols in the shrine makes the game harder via stronger enemies (10 idols in total) and in exchange you get more fragments and exp (up to 70% extra), they can be turned off/on in the bastion.
You can die twice (3 with distillery bonuses) max, then you have the choice to turn all idols off or restart with them on. Falling off the map takes away aprox. 10% of your hp. You respawn again, while invulnerable for a bit, you can't move and melee monsters may cut espace routes.
Each area biome has it's own enemies with some exceptions. There are color swaps and size variations on each type of enemy. Each variation has 1 attack pattern.
These variations include: Charged attacks, faster attacks, ranged attacks, unblockeable attacks, homing projectiles, etc.
There are around 13 types of enemies with ones having 4 variations and 4 unique ones that seem to be bosses (not more challenging than the rest of enemies and still have 1 attack pattern, but speed up as they're dying)
Subjective
Nice and memorable.  Overall the music is something you end up remembering in good light even if the short game doesn't allow all of it to shine.
May not be an extra: Adquiring mementos and clearing the gauntlets are the only ways of knowing more about the world of bastion and it's characters. But since this is something you can do as part of a regular play it may not be an extra.
NG+ allows you keep all the weapons and bonuses you unlocked in your last game but other than the challenge of beating the game again and clearing the gauntlets ( a new 1 appears  in NG+) with all idols on (last 2 idols can only be gotten on NG+), there isn't much more to do.

In short, Miscreated is an enjoyable game, if you are looking for a survival game to play and enjoy with friends for a reasonable amount of time, I highly recommend this one, and I will elaborate why in the rest of the review.
What follows is what I believe to be a fair assessment of Miscreated in the 60 hours of gameplay I've sunk into it. This is by no means my favourite game, but for what it is and what it aims to achieve, I think it ticks all of the right boxes with a few speedbumps along the way.
Miscreated is a Survival RPG/Sandbox game where the primary goal above all else is to make your character survive through whatever means you choose. Be it slaughtering all players you come across and taking their equipment or playing friendly, bartering and trading goods and avoiding combat altogether, the former of which is considerably more common. The basis of the game is nothing we haven't seen before, but whether or not Miscreated does it better than the other Survival games on the market is purely down to preference. Miscreated, or at least in my experience, is notably more faster when trying to get into some PvP action than its competitors. I have no trouble logging in, moving to a town or settlement and finding an armed player to engage in combat with. If you are looking for a game with easy to find player versus player, this game is suitable. Below I've compiled a fairly basic list of pros and cons so you have a general idea of what to expect when playing Miscreated if you choose to purchase it.
Pros:
-Loot seems evenly distributed in all areas, you actually have to search for your items as they can be hidden in cabinets or drawers which adds an element of satisfaction when finding items you need.
-Combat is easy to come across, but it is also just as easy to avoid combat altogether, which i've found produces an even balance between PvP players and PvE players.
-There are many private whitelisted communities and servers that you can get involved with should you want a specific playstyle that is enforced by a whitelisted server.
-Playing with friends isn't too difficult as navigating the map is quite simple and it doesn't take a massive amount of time to get to a specific place.
-Vehicles can be a huge help when traversing the map, it uses a parts system which means you actively have to search for the parts you need as well as gasoline.
:That isn't a full list of pros, there are many others but I am summarising key points that come to mind:
Cons:
-Weapons are not balanced, nor are they entirely fair in terms of their damage. Certain weapons, such as the Handguns, take a significant amount of ammunition (which can be hard to find) to bring down a fully kitted player, and most lean towards being the most accurate, instead of who shoots first.
-The mutants, while a threat in high numbers, are still noticeably stupid, which was only slightly mitigated by the new AI system implemented fairly recently.
-This may be just me, but vehicles, while they are satisfying to repair and drive, are simply not spawning. Either certain groups of players are hoarding them all in bases or they do not spawn at all.
-Base building, while definitely a cool feature, is rendered pointless by the lack of a decent storage system. Because of this, loot has almost no value, as it cannot be stored in significant quantities.
-Friendly players are somewhat rare to come across as most have migrated to PvE communities. (This isn't a con for me but if you're worried about being killed I'd stay away from public servers altogether.)
In conclusion, I personally do think Miscreated is a fun game to play, I even enjoy it solo, but recently certain issues have come up regarding the lack of the development team's involvement with the game's community. I've always had issues with certain moderators for this game's community which led me to being banned from the community group chat (which i still find pretty funny tbh lmao) but if you're not fussed about anything like that, I completely recommend you play Miscreated, because I've enjoyed my time in it, and I'm sure anybody interested in survival games will too.

Isaac and his mother lived alone in a small house on a hill. Isaac kept to himself, drawing pictures, and playing with his toys, as his mom watched christian broadcasts on the television.
Life was simple, and they were both happy. That was until the day Isaac's mom heard a voice from above;
"Your son has become corrupted by sin! He needs to be saved!"
"I will do my best to save him, my lord" his mother replied, Rushing into Isaac's room, removing all that was evil from his life.
Again, the voice called to her; "Isaac's soul is still corrupt! He needs to be cut off from all that is evil in this world, and confess his sins!" "I will follow your instructions lord, I have faith in thee" Isaac's mother replied, as she locked Isaac in his room, away from the evils of the world.
One last time, Isaac's mom heard the voice of god calling to her; "You've done as I've asked, but I still question your devotion to me. To prove your faith, I will ask one more thing of you"
"Yes lord, anything" Isaac's mother begged. "To prove your love and devotion, I require a sacrifice, your son Isaac will be this sacrifice. Go into his room, and end his life as an offering to me to prove you love me above all else"
"Yes lord" she replied, grabbing a butcher's knife from the kitchen.
Isaac, watching through a crack in his door, trembled in fear.
Scrambling around his room to find a hiding place, he noticed a trap door to the basement, hidden under his rug.
Without hesitation, he flung open the hatch, just as his mother burst through his door, and threw himself down, into the unknown depths below.
...
Isaac was cornered. his mother, fueled with the desire to serve her god, was bearing down on Isaac.
"I will do as I'm told, my lord. I love you above all else" Isaac's mother repeated to herself.
This was the end of the line for Isaac, his mother was far too strong for him.
But just as he accepted his fate, god intervened, sending an angel down from above to stop his mother's hand.
And just like that, it was over.

I do really like this game, and I have gotten my fair share out of it, but now i'm coming back to write a review.
As you can probably see, i've spent a good deal of time in this game. It is a really well made game, for the most part, but to be honest, it's just not
When I played it at first, for the first long time I thought it was great, and the game definitely is worth the money, but as time went on I realized this game really isn't that fun. It is a perfect example of a mile wide and an inch deep. There is so much stuff you can do, but not much of it is varied. There is so much for you to see, but after awhile that gets old too, and it takes a long time to do it as well. There are tons of cool little dungeons and buildings on planets, but it takes ages to find good ones and when you do find one they do... Next to nothing. With recent updates you can get crew for your ship and villages have quests, but they're all cardboard cutout carachters and quests. Not very interesting.
My main problem is the combat system. It's awful. It feels super damn clunky and nowhere near satisfying. Long cooldowns, unsmooth movements, and the monsters you fight are borderline childish levels of cartoon. The boss fights feel the same way.
This game is, still, in my opinion, amazing. You can upgrade your ship, furnish your ship, build colonies, explore the galaxy, play as any number of different races all with distinct backstories and traits, but all in all it's just a wandering simulator with furniture. Don't even get me started and the insanely boring mining.
I want to love this game soooo damn badly. I love the lore, the races, and the graphics, for the most part, apeal to me. I just want to praise it's everything, but to be honest, it's not amazing at everything.
This is the game that could have been Terraria 8.0, but sadly, it's just not there. I'd actually reccomend terraria over this, because while terraria is only a couple inches wide, it's a hell of a lot more deep, the mchanics like combat feel much more solid, and the game just feels more satisfying to play. Still, for 20 bucks you can try it out for yourself, the mostly finished version too, so you get to see the good stuff before you get bored. I wasn't that lucky.
If you do get it though, I strongly suggest getting the Avali race mod. It's kinda complicated to install (you need a race extender mod first) but it totally worth it. Favorite race by far.

Starbound is an indi-game focussing on exploration!!!! Take your time, don't rush the quests, design your planet and make it to your home! There are various possibilities to decorate and build things.
The game is about learning to survive and make a comfortable life in an endless universe.
Players, searching for action, combat, war / pvp / an absolute amazing Skyrim-like storyline are totally wrong here!
Starbounds strengths are the open world - Robinson Crusoe - themed surviving, building, living, trading and exploring aspects.
Friends of collecting stuff are here at the right place. You can tame animals, collect ancient fossiles, bugs etc...
To sum up:
i like this game alot, the possibilites are really amazing and the atmosphere with it's genious-soundtracks is overwhealming.
For  a 15 $ - game it is totally worth to buy - but just for the right kind of players like me.

This is my second time through this game. I originally purchased it when it first came out on consoles. If you have a short attention span and do not like long periods of plot between short periods of action, be warned that the first third of this game will make you pull your hair out.
You have one intro mission to get you used to the controls, then you're whisked away to the longest segment of character development/scene setting location I've ever witnessed in a video game. If you choose to do everything in the game, you can be at this point of the game for literally hours without using a gun advancing the mission.
I recommend breaking this part up into smaller bites. Do two or three things, leave and do one mission, then come back and do two or three things.
Now that I got that off my chest, this game and its plot are both amazing. After a really slow start, this game ends with a bang that will make you want to throw your money at the sequel.
If you love Star Trek, you'll love Mass Effect. It has deep plots, nice cultural backgrounds of its aliens, and plenty of decision making that will make you feel like you are shaping the universe.
